CBC (Complete Blood Count).name: CBC (Complete Blood Count)
CBC (Complete Blood Count).about: The CBC (Complete Blood Count) test provides important information about the blood components, including red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets. This test helps screen overall health, detect various medical conditions, and monitor treatment response.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. In Symptomatic Individuals
Fatigue or weakness
Persistent fever
Dizziness or lightheadedness
Pale skin or shortness of breath
Frequent infections
Easy bruising or bleeding
B. In High-Risk Groups
Individuals with a family history of blood disorders (e.g., thalassemia, leukemia)
Individuals on long-term chemotherapy or immunosuppressive therapy
Individuals with iron, vitamin B12, or folate deficiency risk
C. In Special Populations
Pregnant women (to detect anemia or infections)
Children (to assess growth-related nutritional status)
Elderly individuals (to monitor for age-related hematologic changes)
D. In Individuals With Lifestyle-Related Risks
Chronic smokers or alcohol user
Individuals with poor dietary habits or undernutrition
E. In Individuals With Certain Health Conditions
Anemia (iron deficiency, hemolytic, aplastic, etc.)
Infections (bacterial or viral)
Bleeding or clotting disorders
Blood cancers like leukemia or lymphoma
Autoimmune diseases
F. In Routine Follow-Ups
As a part of routine health screening
To track the response to treatment for anemia or infections

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Complete Hemogram (CBC & ESR).name: Complete Hemogram (CBC & ESR)
Complete Hemogram (CBC & ESR).about: The Complete Hemogram (CBC & ESR) test includes a complete blood count (CBC) test and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) test. The CBC test provides information about blood cells, and the ESR test determines the presence of inflammation in the body. Together, these help assess your overall health.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To monitor your overall health as a part of routine checkups.
If you have symptoms such as weakness, fatigue, or fever.
To help identify diseases such as anemia (low number of red blood cells), immune system disorders, blood cancers, bleeding disorders, etc.
To detect the presence of inflammation induced by infections, tumors, or autoimmune illnesses.
To monitor the effects of treatments known to affect blood cells, such as chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
To evaluate the treatment response of inflammatory diseases.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate).name: ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate)
ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate).about: The ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate) Test measures the speed at which your red blood cells settle in a test tube. It specifically measures the rate over one hour. This test helps detect and monitor underlying inflammation in the body.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. As General Screening
To detect inflammation or infection when symptoms are unclear
As part of a general health checkup for chronic illness monitoring
B. If You Have Symptoms. such as:
Persistent fever, fatigue, or generalized weakness
Headaches, especially with scalp tenderness
Jaw pain (suggestive of temporal arteritis)
Muscle or joint pain without an obvious cause
Unexplained weight loss or general malaise
C. For Monitoring
To monitor disease progression or treatment response in chronic conditions such as:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA)
Polymyalgia rheumatica
Tuberculosis
Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

Hb (Hemoglobin).name: Hb (Hemoglobin)
Hb (Hemoglobin).about: The Hb (Hemoglobin) Test measures the amount of hemoglobin in your blood, a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen throughout the body. This test helps detect conditions like anemia, polycythemia, and other blood-related disorders. It is often done as part of a complete blood count (CBC) or during a routine health checkup.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. As General Screening
To assess overall health as part of a complete blood count (CBC)
To detect early signs of anemia or other hematologic conditions
B. If You Have Symptoms, such as:
Persistent tiredness, dizziness, or shortness of breath
Pale skin or nail beds
Unexplained bleeding or bruising
C. For Monitoring
To monitor disease progression or treatment response in conditions such as:
Iron deficiency anemia
Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency
Chronic kidney disease
Bone marrow disorders

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Platelet Count.name: Platelet Count
Platelet Count.about: The Platelet Count test measures the average number of platelets in the blood. Platelets are tiny, colorless blood cells that play a critical role in blood clotting. This test helps detect or monitor conditions that cause excessive bleeding or clotting. It is often done as part of a complete blood count test that also measures other types of blood cells.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of a complete blood count test to monitor your overall health.
In case of signs and symptoms of bleeding disorders, such as easy bruising and prolonged bleeding.
To detect and monitor clotting disorders.
To detect or monitor diseases affecting platelets, such as dengue or inflammatory diseases.
Before surgery, if you have a personal or family history of bleeding disorders.
To monitor platelet count if you are taking blood-thinning medicines, underwent chemotherapy treatment, or a platelet transfusion procedure.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Peripheral Smear Examination.name: Peripheral Smear Examination
Peripheral Smear Examination.about: The Peripheral Smear Examination test is used to evaluate your blood cells (red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets) and note any abnormal differences in their size, shape, or other physical appearances, such as those seen in various anemias, sickle cell disease, thalassemia, or other disorders.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To monitor your overall health as part of routine health checkups.
When a complete blood count (CBC) test shows abnormal results.
If you have symptoms such as weakness, fatigue, or fever.
For more information about your bone marrow and blood cells if you are going for a stem cell transplant.
To identify diseases like anemia (low number of red blood cells), immune system disorders, blood cancers, bleeding disorders, etc.
To monitor the effects of treatments that are known to affect blood cells, such as chemotherapy or radiotherapy.

prepInfo.title: Give brief clinical history.

Reticulocyte Count.name: Reticulocyte Count
Reticulocyte Count.about: The Reticulocyte Count is a blood test that measures the number of reticulocytes (immature red blood cells). It helps evaluate bone marrow function and assess the body’s ability to produce red blood cells, providing crucial insights into various blood disorders and conditions affecting red blood cell production.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: Diagnose and evaluate the cause of anemia.
Monitor the body’s response to treatment for anemia.
Assess bone marrow function.
Evaluate recovery from blood loss or hemolysis (destruction of red blood cells).
Monitor patients undergoing treatment for conditions that affect red blood cell production, such as chemotherapy.
Help differentiate between types of anemia, such as those caused by iron deficiency versus those resulting from chronic disease.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Total Leukocyte Count.name: Total Leukocyte Count
Total Leukocyte Count.about: The Total Leukocyte Count, also known as TLC test measures the number of leukocytes, also known as white blood cells (WBCs), in the blood. This test helps detect infection, inflammation, and bone marrow disorders. It is often done as part of a complete blood count test that also measures other types of blood cells.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As a part of routine checkups to monitor your overall health.
As a part of a complete blood count (CBC) test.
To help detect conditions that decrease WBC count, like bone marrow disorders.
To help detect infections and inflammation.
To monitor the response to certain medical treatments that can affect the immune system, including chemotherapy.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Differential Leukocyte Count.name: Differential Leukocyte Count
Differential Leukocyte Count.about: The Differential Leukocyte Count test measures the percentage of each type of leukocyte or white blood cell (WBC) in the blood. This test is a key indicator of WBC abnormalities, such as infections, inflammation, allergies, bone marrow disorders, or autoimmune diseases. It is also done as part of a complete blood count test that also measures other types of blood cells.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of routine checkups to monitor your overall health.
As part of a (CBC) complete blood count test.
To detect infection, inflammation, and allergies.
To detect white blood cell disorders, such as leukopenia, leukocytosis, or leukemia.
To detect bone marrow disorders affecting WBC count.
To monitor bone marrow function.
To monitor treatments affecting the number of WBCs, such as chemotherapy or radiotherapy.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Absolute Eosinophil Count.name: Absolute Eosinophil Count
Absolute Eosinophil Count.about: An Absolute Eosinophil Count test measures the number of eosinophils, a type of white blood cell, in the blood. This test is a key indicator of certain allergic diseases, infections, etc. in the body. It is often done as part of a complete blood count test that also measures other types of blood cells.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of a complete blood count test to monitor your overall health.
In case of signs or symptoms suggestive of an allergy to one or more substances, such as red itchy eyes, coughing, nasal congestion, asthma, dermatitis, or abdominal pain.
To identify the cause of an inflammation or infection.
To detect the early stages of Cushing’s disease.
To detect a rare disease known as acute hypereosinophilic syndrome.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Blood Group ABO & Rh Factor.name: Blood Group ABO & Rh Factor
Blood Group ABO & Rh Factor.about: The Blood Group ABO & Rh Factor helps determine your blood type (A, B, AB, and O) and Rhesus (Rh) factor (positive or negative). Knowing your blood group is important for safe blood transfusions, organ transplants, and pregnancy care, as it helps ensure compatibility and prevents complications.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To identify the type of blood group and determine Rh compatibility.
To ensure compatibility between the donor and recipient in the case of blood transfusion.
To identify potential Rh incompatibility between the mother and the baby during pregnancy.
To ensure compatibility between the organ donor's and recipient's blood types during organ transplantation.
To facilitate rapid and accurate transfusion of blood components during an emergency.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Serum Ferritin.name: Serum Ferritin
Serum Ferritin.about: The Serum Ferritin Test test measures the ferritin protein level in the blood. Ferritin is a protein that stores iron in the body. Hence, this test helps determine how much iron is stored in your body. It also helps detect diseases such as iron deficiency anemia as well as the nutritional status of an individual.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Serum Ferritin Test test can be done:
To diagnose or confirm iron deficiency anemia, a condition characterized by low levels of iron in the body.
To monitor iron levels in individuals with chronic diseases, iron overload disorders, or those receiving iron therapy.
To assess organ function, particularly the liver, detect or monitor diseases like liver disease, restless leg syndrome, adult-onset Still’s disease, etc.
To determine the body’s capacity to store iron.
To assess the nutritional status, particularly concerning iron intake.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Iron, Serum.name: Iron, Serum
Iron, Serum.about: An Iron, Serum Test measures the amount of iron present in your body. This test is usually done if someone is suspected of iron deficiency or overload. It may also be done as a part of routine health checkups and as a follow-up if a person has abnormal iron levels and is undergoing treatment for the same.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of routine health checkups to estimate iron levels in your body.
If you have signs or symptoms of iron-deficiency anemia, like pallor, fatigue, weakness, or headaches.
If your CBC test results show that your hemoglobin and hematocrit are low and RBCs are smaller and paler than normal, which usually suggests iron-deficiency anemia.
If you have signs or symptoms of increased accumulation of iron in the body, like joint pain, abdominal pain, fatigue, or loss of body hair.
To monitor ongoing treatment for iron deficiency anemia or iron overload.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.
Avoid iron supplements for at least 24 hours prior to sample collection.

Total Iron Binding Capacity.name: Total Iron Binding Capacity
Total Iron Binding Capacity.about: The Total Iron Binding Capacity Test test helps to assess the ability of blood to attach to iron and transport it to various parts of the body. It shows the total binding capacity of transferrin, the protein in the blood that is essential to bind iron and facilitate its movement in the body. Doctors use this test to help determine iron deficiency or iron overload.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of iron studies.
To determine the capacity of the blood to transport iron.
In case of abnormal results hemoglobin and hematocrit on complete blood count.
In case of signs and symptoms of iron deficiency such as chronic fatigue/tiredness, dizziness, weakness, headaches, pale skin (pallor), etc.

In case of signs and symptoms of iron overload such as joint pain, fatigue, weakness, weight loss, lack of energy, abdominal pain, loss of sex drive, organ damage, such as in the heart and/or liver, etc.
To monitor ongoing treatment for iron deficiency anemia or iron overload.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.
Avoid iron supplements for at least 24 hours prior to sample collection.

Serum Iron Studies Basic.name: Serum Iron Studies Basic
Serum Iron Studies Basic.about: The Serum Iron Studies Basic is a set of blood tests that measures the amount of iron and iron-binding proteins in the blood. This test helps detect conditions associated with iron deficiency or iron overload. It may be done as a follow-up to certain routine rests or during anemia therapy.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of routine health checkups to estimate iron levels in your body.
If you have signs or symptoms of iron-deficiency anemia, like pallor, fatigue, weakness, or headaches.
If your CBC test results show that your hemoglobin and hematocrit are low and RBCs are smaller and paler than usual. This usually suggests iron deficiency anemia.
If you have signs or symptoms of increased accumulation of iron in the body, like joint pain, abdominal pain, fatigue, or loss of body hair.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.
Avoid iron supplements for at least 24 hours prior to sample collection.

Transferrin.name: Transferrin
Transferrin.about: The Transferrin Test test measures the amount of transferrin, a protein that binds and transports iron in your blood. This test is commonly used to assess iron metabolism and to diagnose conditions related to iron deficiency or overload.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of routine iron studies to evaluate iron transport and metabolism.
If you exhibit signs or symptoms of iron deficiency anemia, such as fatigue, weakness, or pale skin.
To further investigate the cause of abnormal findings from other iron studies or CBC tests that indicate potential iron imbalances.
To assess iron overload conditions, particularly if there are symptoms like general weakness, joint pain, irregular heartbeat, abdominal discomfort, unexplained weight loss.
To monitor the effectiveness of treatment for conditions related to iron deficiency or overload.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

Thalassemia Screening Profile.name: Thalassemia Screening Profile
Thalassemia Screening Profile.about: The Thalassemia Screening Profile comprises a group of blood tests that help diagnose and monitor thalassemia, a genetic blood disorder characterized by the production of defective hemoglobin. This test helps evaluate parameters like complete blood counts, hemoglobin variants, and iron levels, which are essential for diagnosing and managing the condition.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To identify the presence and the type of thalassemia in symptomatic individuals.
To determine if an individual is a carrier of thalassemia traits (genes), which is important for family planning.
To distinguish thalassemia from other types of anemia, such as iron deficiency anemia.
As a part of prenatal screening to assess the risk of thalassemia in unborn children when parents are known carriers.
To monitor hemoglobin levels and overall health in individuals with thalassemia.
To help guide informed treatment decisions in individuals diagnosed with thalassemia.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.
Record the date of birth, sex, race and religion on the test request form for sample collection.
A duly filled HPLC form is mandatory.
Avoid iron supplements for at least 24 hours prior to sample collection.
Clinical history is required.

G6PD - Quantitative Reflex Qualitative.name: G6PD - Quantitative Reflex Qualitative
G6PD - Quantitative Reflex Qualitative.about: The G6PD - Quantitative Reflex Qualitative Test is a blood test that helps measure the activity of the enzyme glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) in red blood cells. G6PD deficiency is a genetic disorder that can cause hemolytic anemia, particularly in response to specific triggers like medications, foods, or infections.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To diagnose G6PD deficiency, especially in individuals with unexplained hemolytic anemia.
To evaluate if hemolytic anemia is due to G-6-PD deficiency, especially after exposure to certain drugs, infections, or foods (e.g., fava beans).
To help identify the cause of neonatal jaundice.
To monitor individuals from high-risk ethnic backgrounds who may be at risk of hemolytic episodes.
To assess G6PD enzyme activity before administering medications that may trigger hemolysis.
To assess the effectiveness of treatments for conditions related to G-6-PD deficiency, such as during or after a hemolytic episode.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Sickling Test.name: Sickling Test
Sickling Test.about: The Sickling Test is a blood test used to identify both sickle cell disease and sickle cell trait caused by hemoglobin S (an abnormal form of hemoglobin). The test looks for changes in the morphology of the red blood cells (RBCs) by microscopy to detect sickle cell anemia and to find people who carry the sickle cell trait (gene).

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To diagnose sickle cell anemia.
To identify whether a person carries the sickle cell trait.
To investigate the causes of unexplained anemia or pain episodes.
To screen newborns for sickle cell disease.
As a part of pre-martial testing to screen for sickle cell disease in high-risk population.
To monitor individuals with known sickle cell disease to evaluate the progression of the condition and manage treatment.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

FBS (Fasting Blood Sugar).name: FBS (Fasting Blood Sugar)
FBS (Fasting Blood Sugar).about: The FBS (Fasting Blood Sugar) Test measures the glucose (sugar) level in the blood after overnight fasting. This test is done when a person experiences symptoms of high or low blood sugar levels or to assess a person’s risk for diabetes. It is often done as part of a routine health checkup.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. As General Screening (American Diabetes Association (ADA) Recommendations, 2025)
All adults who are 35 years or above
Children and adults under 35 years with risk factors
Overweight/obesity
Family history of diabetes
High blood pressure (BP), cholesterol, and heart disease
Sedentary lifestyle
History of gestational diabetes or polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
B. If You Have Symptoms
Frequent thirst, urination, or extreme hunger
Unexplained weight loss, fatigue, or blurred vision
Slow-healing wounds or frequent infections
C. High-Risk Groups (Monitoring)
Prediabetes (FBS 100-125 mg/dL ) - Test every 1–2 years
Diabetes (FBS ≥ 126 mg/dL) - Test every 3–6 months for management
Individuals with HIV (before starting, when switching, and 3–6 months after antiviral therapy, then annually if FBS results are normal)
Women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) - Test every 3 year

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting (8-12 hrs) is required. Do not eat or drink anything except water before the test.

PPBS (Postprandial Blood Sugar).name: PPBS (Postprandial Blood Sugar)
PPBS (Postprandial Blood Sugar).about: The PPBS (Postprandial Blood Sugar) Test measures the levels of blood sugar (glucose) typically, two hours after eating a meal. It helps assess the risk of diabetes and monitor the effectiveness of ongoing treatment. It is often done as part of routine health checkups or when there are symptoms of abnormal blood sugar levels.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. As General Screening (American Diabetes Association (ADA) Recommendations, 2025)
All adults who are 35 years or above
Children and adults under 35 years with risk factors
Overweight/obesity
Family history of diabetes
High blood pressure (BP), cholesterol, and heart disease
Sedentary lifestyle
History of gestational diabetes or polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
B. If You Have Symptoms
Frequent thirst, urination, or extreme hunger
Unexplained weight loss, fatigue, or blurred vision
Slow-healing wounds or frequent infections
C. High-Risk Groups (Monitoring)
Prediabetes (FBS 100-125 mg/dL) - Test every 1–2 years
Diabetes (FBS ≥ 126 mg/dL) - Test every 3–6 months for management
Individuals with HIV (before starting, when switching, and 3–6 months after antiviral therapy, then annually if FBS results are normal)
Women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) - Test every 3 years

prepInfo.title: Sample to be given exactly 2 hours after starting meal or as advised by the physician.
Please note that it is mandatory to abide by the pre-scheduled sample collection time, as this will help us ensure the accuracy of the test results.

RBS (Random Blood Sugar).name: RBS (Random Blood Sugar)
RBS (Random Blood Sugar).about: The RBS (Random Blood Sugar) Test measures the glucose (sugar) level in your blood at any time of the day, regardless of when you last ate. This test helps assess how well your body manages glucose throughout the day.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. As General Screening (American Diabetes Association (ADA) Recommendations, 2025)
To detect diabetes in individuals showing symptoms of high blood sugar (hyperglycemia).
To support diagnosis when a random plasma glucose level is ≥ 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) in a person with classic symptoms of diabetes.
To monitor known diabetic patients for unexpected glucose fluctuations during routine or hospital visits.
To evaluate glucose control in emergency settings or acute illness, when fasting may not be possible.
B. If You Have Symptoms, such as:
Frequent thirst, urination, or increased appetite
Unexplained weight loss, fatigue, or blurred vision
Slow-healing wounds or frequent infections
C. High-Risk Groups (Monitoring)
Individuals with prediabetes or diagnosed diabetes
Women with gestational diabetes (GDM)

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

HbA1c (Glycosylated Hemoglobin).name: HbA1c (Glycosylated Hemoglobin)
HbA1c (Glycosylated Hemoglobin).about: The HbA1c (Glycosylated Hemoglobin) Test measures the average blood sugar levels over a period of 2 to 3 months. It is used to diagnose diabetes and to monitor individuals undergoing treatment. It is often done as part of routine health checkups.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: An HbA1c test can be done:
A. As General Screening (American Diabetes Association (ADA) Recommendations, 2025)
All adults who are 35 years or older
Children and adults under 35 years with risk factors
Overweight/obesity
Family history of diabetes
High blood pressure (BP), cholesterol, and heart disease
Sedentary lifestyle
History of gestational diabetes or polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
B. If You Have Symptoms, such as:
Frequent thirst or appetite
Excessive urination
Unexplained weight loss, fatigue, or blurred vision
Slow-healing wounds or frequent infections
C. High-Risk Groups (Monitoring)
Prediabetes (HbA1c 5.7% – 6.4%)- Test every 1-2 years
Diabetes (HbA1c ≥ 6.5% on two tests)- Test every 3-6 months for management

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Diabetes Screening (HbA1C & Fasting Suga.name: Diabetes Screening (HbA1C & Fasting Sugar)
Diabetes Screening (HbA1C & Fasting Suga.about: The Diabetes Screening (HbA1C & Fasting Sugar) test includes two blood tests, namely fasting blood sugar level and glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c), that help estimate your blood sugar levels, assess your risk of developing diabetes, and monitor iyour treatment progress. This test is often done as part of a routine health checkup.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of routine health checkups to measure blood glucose levels.
If you have symptoms of high or low blood glucose levels, such as weight gain, weight loss, blurred vision, frequent urge to urinate, or confusion.
To assess the risk of diabetes and prediabetes and monitor diabetes treatment.
To screen pregnant women for gestational diabetes alongside other tests.
If you have a family history of diabetes, are above 45 years, and are overweight.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting (8-12 hrs) is required. Do not eat or drink anything except water before the test.

Glucose 2 hrs Post 75g Load.name: Glucose 2 hrs Post 75g Load
Glucose 2 hrs Post 75g Load.about: The Glucose 2 hrs Post 75g Load Test is a blood test used to diagnose diabetes and prediabetes. This test involves drinking a 75-gram glucose solution and measuring blood sugar levels two hours after starting intake of glucose load to ensure they are within a healthy range, providing valuable insights into glucose metabolism.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To diagnose type 2 diabetes and prediabetes by assessing the body's glucose metabolism.
For individuals with risk factors like obesity, a sedentary lifestyle, or a family history of diabetes.
When there is an abnormal result on a fasting blood sugar test or HbA1c test.
To evaluate the effectiveness of diabetes management plans, including lifestyle changes and medications.

prepInfo.title: Patient takes 75 g glucose and sample will be collected 2 hour after oral administration of glucose.

Insulin, Fasting.name: Insulin, Fasting
Insulin, Fasting.about: The Insulin, Fasting Test test checks the levels of insulin hormone in the blood after fasting for 8-12 hours. This hormone is made by the pancreas, which controls blood sugar levels. This test helps check how well your body is using insulin. It also helps determine your risk for insulin resistance (where the body does not respond properly to insulin).

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Insulin, Fasting Test test can be done:
A. If You Have Symptoms (hypoglycemic symptoms)
Sweating
Feeling shaky or jittery
Arrhythmia (a problem with the rate or rhythm of your heartbeat)
Confusion
Dizziness
Headache
Hunger
B. If there are risk factors
Prediabetes
Type 2 diabetes
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
Heart disease
Acanthosis nigricans (an abnormal skin condition), heart disease, or metabolic syndrome
C. In special population
Undergone a glucose blood test (if test results are low)
Undergone pancreatic surgery

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting (8-12 hrs) is required. Do not eat or drink anything except water before the test.

Insulin - Post Prandial.name: Insulin - Post Prandial
Insulin - Post Prandial.about: An Insulin - Post Prandial Test measures the level of insulin in your blood after a meal, typically two hours after a meal. This test is done when symptoms like increased thirst or urination, appetite changes, weakness, weight changes, tingling or numbness in the hands or legs, etc. are experienced by an individual.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To determine the cause of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia).
To determine the proper production of insulin by the pancreas.
To monitor the condition of people with type 2 diabetes.
To determine if insulin resistance in cells is the cause of hyperglycemia (high blood sugar).
To determine if insulin supplementation is necessary.
To determine the presence of insulin-producing tumors (insulinomas) in the beta cells of the pancreas.

prepInfo.title: Sample to be given exactly 2 hours after starting meal or as advised by the physician.

C-Peptide, Fasting.name: C-Peptide, Fasting
C-Peptide, Fasting.about: The C-Peptide, Fasting Test test measures the level of C-peptide in the blood after a period of 8 to 12 hours of fasting. This test evaluates insulin production by the pancreas and helps understand, monitor, or treat disorders such as hypoglycemia (low blood sugar), diabetes, etc.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To help evaluate the ability of the pancreas to produce insulin.
To diagnose diabetes and distinguish between type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
To monitor the effectiveness of diabetes treatments, such as insulin therapy.
To assess insulin resistance, a common problem in type 2 diabetes.
To provide insights into the functioning of the beta cells in the pancreas, which produce insulin.

To monitor how well the insulinomas (pancreatic tumors) are responding to the treatment as decreasing levels of C-peptide indicate a positive response to treatment while increasing levels may suggest tumor recurrence.
To help evaluate an individual diagnosed with metabolic syndrome.
To determine if someone with diabetes may benefit from insulin therapy and at what dosage.
To assess the success of pancreatic islet cell transplants, which aim to restore insulin production, ensuring the treatment is effective and continues to be successful.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting (8-12 hrs) is required. Do not eat or drink anything except water before the test.

HOMA IR; Insulin Resistance Index.name: HOMA IR; Insulin Resistance Index
HOMA IR; Insulin Resistance Index.about: The HOMA IR; Insulin Resistance Index Test is a group of blood tests used to assess an individual's insulin resistance. Insulin resistance is a condition where cells fail to respond effectively to insulin. The resistance is calculated using fasting insulin and glucose levels.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To assess insulin resistance by providing insights into the body's ability to respond to insulin.
To identify individuals at risk of developing type 2 diabetes by detecting early signs of insulin resistance.
As a part of the diagnostic criteria to diagnose metabolic syndrome.
To monitor the effectiveness of interventions such as lifestyle changes or medication therapy for insulin resistance over time.
In research settings, to investigate the role of insulin resistance in conditions, including obesity, PCOS, and cardiovascular diseases.
To help classify individuals into different risk categories based on their insulin sensitivity.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting (8-12 hrs) is required. Do not eat or drink anything except water before the test.

Fructosamine.name: Fructosamine
Fructosamine.about: The Fructosamine Test assesses the level of fructosamine, a compound that is formed when glucose combines with protein, in the blood. Just like HbA1C, this test helps to determine glycemic control in diabetic patients over a span of 2 to 3 weeks. It is the best test to assess effectiveness of diet or medication after a few weeks rather than months.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To monitor short-term blood sugar control in individuals with diabetes.
Evaluate the effectiveness of diabetes treatment or lifestyle changes.
Help guide treatment decisions, particularly in individuals with fluctuating blood sugar levels.
Detect and manage high blood sugar (hyperglycemia) or other conditions related to blood sugar.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation required

GAD-65 AntibodyType I Diabetes.name: GAD-65 AntibodyType I Diabetes
GAD-65 AntibodyType I Diabetes.about: The GAD-65 AntibodyType I Diabetes test measures the amount of antibodies that target the glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) enzyme in the pancreas and nervous system. These antibodies are linked to the autoimmune response that can cause type 1 diabetes. The test helps diagnose early-stage type 1 diabetes and assess the risk of developing diabetes.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To help diagnose type 1 diabetes in people with symptoms like thirst, frequent urination, weight loss, fatigue, etc.
To differentiate between type 1 and type 2 diabetes (as GAD antibodies are more common in type 1).
To determine the risk of developing type 1 diabetes or a slow progressive form of autoimmune diabetes called latent autoimmune diabetes of adulthood (LADA).
To assess the risk of diabetes in people with a family history of type 1 diabetes or other autoimmune diseases.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Thyroid Profile Total (T3, T4 & TSH).name: Thyroid Profile Total (T3, T4 & TSH)
Thyroid Profile Total (T3, T4 & TSH).about: The Thyroid Profile Total (T3, T4 & TSH) is a group of blood tests that measure the levels of three key hormones: total triiodothyronine (T3​), total thyroxine (T4​), and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH). This test helps your doctor check how well your thyroid gland is working.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. As General Screening:
To check thyroid function in newborns (usually within the first five days of birth) to detect congenital/neonatal hyperthyroidism
For individuals with autoimmune diseases (like type 1 diabetes or rheumatoid arthritis), they have a higher risk of autoimmune thyroid issues.
For women who are pregnant or planning a pregnancy, as normal thyroid function is vital for fetal development
B. If You Have Symptoms
To diagnose an underactive (hypothyroidism) or overactive (hyperthyroidism) thyroid when symptoms are present
C. High-Risk Groups (Monitoring)
To monitor individuals already diagnosed with a thyroid condition (like Hashimoto's or Graves' disease) to ensure treatment is working
To evaluate patients with a personal or family history of thyroid disease or those who have had thyroid surgery or radiation treatment

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.
Do not stop taking your thyroid medications on the day of the test unless otherwise advised by the doctor.

Thyroid Profile Free (FT3, FT4 & TSH).name: Thyroid Profile Free (FT3, FT4 & TSH)
Thyroid Profile Free (FT3, FT4 & TSH).about: The Thyroid Profile Free (FT3, FT4 & TSH) is a group of blood tests that measure the levels of free form of thyroid hormones. These tests are used to check how well the thyroid gland is functioning by measuring the levels of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), free thyroxine (FT4), and free triiodothyronine (FT3).

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Thyroid Profile Free (FT3, FT4 & TSH) is done:
As part of routine health checkups to monitor your thyroid health.
To evaluate symptoms that can be caused by an imbalance in thyroid hormone levels.
To diagnose thyroid disease, such as hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, Grave’s disease, thyroiditis, or Hashimoto’s disease.
To monitor treatment efficacy for thyroid disease.
To detect an underactive thyroid gland in newborn babies.
To evaluate and monitor treatments of other disorders, such as thyroid nodules and pituitary or hypothalamus gland disorders.
To investigate the cause of infertility.

prepInfo.title: Do not stop taking your thyroid medications on the day of the test unless otherwise advised by the doctor.
No special preparation is required.

FT3 & FT4 (Free T3 & Free T4).name: FT3 & FT4 (Free T3 & Free T4)
FT3 & FT4 (Free T3 & Free T4).about: An FT3 & FT4 (Free T3 & Free T4) test measures the amount of free form of triiodothyronine (FT3) and thyroxine (FT4) hormones in the blood. This test helps evaluate the functioning of the thyroid gland and detect possible thyroid disorders, including hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To measure the levels of free T3 and T4 hormones in the body.
As part of a thyroid profile test along with a TSH test.
To evaluate symptoms suggestive of an imbalance in thyroid hormone levels, such as fatigue, weight loss, hair loss, and changes to heart rate.
To diagnose and monitor the treatment of hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism.
To detect an underactive thyroid gland in newborn babies.
To evaluate other disorders, such as thyroid nodules, goiters, and pituitary or hypothalamus gland disorders.

prepInfo.title: Do not stop taking your thyroid medications on the day of the test unless otherwise advised by the doctor.

Triiodothyronine - Total (T3).name: Triiodothyronine - Total (T3)
Triiodothyronine - Total (T3).about: The Triiodothyronine - Total (T3) Test test measures the level of total triiodothyronine hormone in the blood. This test helps assess overall thyroid function and detect possible thyroid disorders. It is also performed in combination with total T4 and TSH tests as part of a thyroid profile total test.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Triiodothyronine - Total (T3) Test test is done:
To measure the levels of total T3 hormone in the body.
As part of a thyroid profile-total along with total T4 and TSH tests.
To evaluate symptoms suggestive of an imbalance in thyroid hormone levels, such as fatigue, weight loss, hair loss, and changes in heart rate.
To diagnose and monitor the treatment of hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism.
To detect an underactive thyroid gland in newborn babies.
To evaluate disorders such as thyroid nodules, goiters, and pituitary or hypothalamus gland disorders.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Thyroxine - Total (T4).name: Thyroxine - Total (T4)
Thyroxine - Total (T4).about: The Thyroxine - Total (T4) Test is a blood test that measures the level of total thyroxine (T4) hormone in the blood. This test helps assess overall thyroid function and detect possible thyroid disorders. It is also performed in combination with total T3 and TSH tests as part of a thyroid profile total test.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Thyroxine - Total (T4) Test test is done:
To measure the levels of total T4 hormone in the body.
As part of a thyroid profile total test along with total T3 and TSH tests.
To evaluate symptoms suggestive of an imbalance in thyroid hormone levels, such as fatigue, weight loss, hair loss, and changes to heart rate.
To diagnose and monitor the treatment of hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism.
To detect an underactive thyroid gland in newborn babies.
To evaluate disorders such as thyroid nodules, goiters, and pituitary or hypothalamus gland disorders.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.
Do not stop taking your thyroid medications on the day of the test unless otherwise advised by the doctor.

Thyroxine - Free (FT4).name: Thyroxine - Free (FT4)
Thyroxine - Free (FT4).about: The Thyroxine - Free (FT4) Test test measures the amount of free form of thyroxine hormone in the blood. This test helps evaluate the functioning of the thyroid gland and detect possible thyroid disorders. It is also performed in combination with free T3 and TSH tests as part of a thyroid profile free test.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To measure the levels of free T4 hormone in the body.
As part of a thyroid profile test along with FT3 and TSH tests.
To evaluate symptoms suggestive of an imbalance in thyroid hormone levels, such as fatigue, weight loss, hair loss, and changes to heart rate.
To diagnose and monitor the treatment of hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism.
To detect an underactive thyroid gland in newborn babies.
To evaluate other disorders, such as thyroid nodules, goiters, and pituitary or hypothalamus gland disorders.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Triiodothyronine - Free (FT3).name: Triiodothyronine - Free (FT3)
Triiodothyronine - Free (FT3).about: The Triiodothyronine - Free (FT3) Test test measures the free triiodothyronine (FT3) hormone level in the blood. This test helps assess overall thyroid function and detect possible thyroid disorders. It is also performed with free T4 and TSH tests as part of a thyroid profile-free test.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To measure the levels of free T3 hormone in the body.
As part of a free thyroid profile along with free T4 and TSH tests.
To evaluate symptoms suggestive of an imbalance in thyroid hormone levels, such as fatigue, weight loss, hair loss, and changes to heart rate.
To diagnose and monitor the treatment of hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism.
To detect an underactive thyroid gland in newborn babies.
To evaluate other disorders, such as thyroid nodules, goiters, and pituitary or hypothalamus gland disorders.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Anti Thyroid Antibodies Panel.name: Anti Thyroid Antibodies Panel
Anti Thyroid Antibodies Panel.about: An Anti Thyroid Antibodies Panel is a blood test that assesses the presence of specific antibodies associated with autoimmune thyroid disorders. These antibodies are directed against thyroid peroxidase and thyroglobulin and are called as anti-thyroid peroxidase (TPO) and anti-thyroglobulin (TG) respectively. These antibodies help us to diagnose and manage autoimmune disorders of thyroid such as Hashimoto’s thyroiditis and Grave’s disease.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To detect specific antibodies associated with autoimmune thyroid disorders.
To assess thyroid health and function, especially in cases where abnormal thyroid levels are detected.
To assess the risk of developing thyroid-related disorders such as hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism.
To differentiate autoimmune disorders of the thyroid, such as Hashimoto’s thyroiditis or Grave’s disease, from other causes of thyroid dysfunction, like non-autoimmune goiter.
To evaluate thyroid involvement in non-thyroid related autoimmune disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
To monitor the autoimmune response over time, especially in individuals with known thyroid conditions or a history of autoimmune thyroid diseases.
To assess the risk of developing autoimmune thyroid disorders , especially in individuals with a family history of autoimmune thyroid diseases.
To monitor the effectiveness of treatment for autoimmune thyroid disorders.
During pregnancy to identify potential risks and complications related to thyroid disorders that may affect both the mother and the baby.
As a part of assessment of infertility.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Thyroglobulin.name: Thyroglobulin
Thyroglobulin.about: The Thyroglobulin Test test is a blood test that measures the level of thyroglobulin, a protein produced only by the thyroid gland. This test is primarily used as a tumor marker for people treated for thyroid cancer. It helps monitor for cancer recurrence and assess the effectiveness of treatment.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To monitor and manage individuals who have undergone thyroidectomy and thyroid cancer treatment.
To detect any recurrence or persistence of thyroid cancer.
To assess the effectiveness of radioactive iodine therapy.
To evaluate for possible metastasis in individuals with thyroid cancer.
To determine if additional treatment or intervention is required for the thyroid gland.
To aid in the management and follow-up of patients with autoimmune thyroid diseases.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

TSH Receptor Antibodies.name: TSH Receptor Antibodies
TSH Receptor Antibodies.about: The TSH Receptor Antibodies test is a blood test that detects the presence of specific proteins called Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH) Receptor Antibodies. These antibodies play an important role in the development and diagnosis of autoimmune thyroid diseases, such as Grave’s disease. They can stimulate or inhibit thyroid hormone production leading to various clinical manifestations.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To confirm the diagnosis of Grave’s disease, the most common cause of hyperthyroidism.
To help differentiate Grave’s disease from other causes of hyperthyroidism, such as toxic multinodular goiter or toxic adenoma.
To assess treatment response against Grave’s disease.
In pregnant women with Grave’s disease, predict the risk of neonatal thyrotoxicosis in the newborn.
To evaluate and manage the development of thyroid eye disease (Grave’s ophthalmology).
To assess the risk of transition to hyperthyroidism in cases of hypothyroidism, particularly Hashimoto’s thyroiditis.
In research settings to better understand autoimmune thyroid diseases and develop new treatment strategies.

prepInfo.title: High Biotin dose (>5 mg/day) should be avoided at least 8 hrs prior to blood collection.

Lipid Profile.name: Lipid Profile
Lipid Profile.about: The Lipid Profile is a group of blood tests that measures different types of fats (such as cholesterol or triglycerides). It helps assess cardiovascular (heart) health, especially in individuals with risk factors like high blood pressure, being overweight, diabetes, etc. This profile is often included in routine or preventive health checkups.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. As General Screening (as per Lipid Association of India (LAI) Guidelines)
All adults ≽ 20 years (every 5 years)
Individuals with risk factors (every 1 to 2 years)
Age (male ≥45 years, female ≥55 years)
Overweight/obesity
Family history of heart disease
High blood pressure (BP)
Low HDL (males <40 mg/dl and females <50 mg/dl)
B. If You Have Symptoms Suggestive of Cardiovascular Problems:
Chest pain or discomfort (especially on exertion)
Shortness of breath
Fatigue or dizziness
Numbness or coldness in the limbs (due to bad circulation)
Sudden vision problems or slurred speech (indicate vascular issues)
C. In Individuals With Lifestyle-Related Risks
Tobacco/smoke
Sedentary lifestyle
Chronic stress
D. For Monitoring
In individuals on lipid-lowering medications (e.g., statins) to monitor treatment response

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting (8-12 hrs) is required. Do not eat or drink anything except water before the test.

Lipid Profile, Non Fasting.name: Lipid Profile, Non Fasting
Lipid Profile, Non Fasting.about: The Lipid Profile, Non Fasting helps measure and monitor the amount of different types of lipids, like cholesterol and triglyceride, in the blood. Your doctor may advise this test to determine your overall cardiovascular health if you have risk factors, such as obesity, diabetes, and high blood pressure. It is usually done as a part of routine health checkups.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of routine health checkups to measure the levels of lipids and cholesterol in the blood.
To determine an individual's risk of developing heart conditions, stroke, and peripheral artery disease.

To monitor the lipids and cholesterol levels in individuals already diagnosed with high cholesterol or cardiovascular disease to ensure that their treatment plans are effective in maintaining healthy cholesterol levels.

To detect early deviations in lipids and cholesterol levels in individuals with a family history of high cholesterol levels or premature heart disease, enabling timely interventions and lifestyle modifications to reduce their risk of cardiovascular complications.
To help diagnose other medical conditions, such as liver disease.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Extended Lipid Profile.name: Extended Lipid Profile
Extended Lipid Profile.about: An Extended Lipid Profile gives detailed insights into different types of cholesterol and fats in your blood, going beyond the standard lipid profile. This test provides a better understanding of your heart health and tells about the risks of heart disease and stroke.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: For a comprehensive assessment of lipid levels and cardiovascular risk.
For a more detailed analysis of the lipid metabolism beyond the basic lipid profile.
To evaluate cardiovascular health and risk factors for heart disease and stroke.
In individuals with risk factors like family history of heart disease, obesity, diabetes, high blood pressure, and prior heart attack or stroke.
To determine an individual's risk of developing cardiovascular diseases such as atherosclerosis, etc.
In Individuals with a previous history of a heart attack, stroke, or other cardiovascular event to monitor their lipid levels closely and adjust their treatment accordingly.
To evaluate treatment response for patients undergoing lipid-lowering therapy or other interventions for cardiovascular risk reduction.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting (8-12 hrs) is required. Do not eat or drink anything except water before the test.

Cholesterol - Total.name: Cholesterol - Total
Cholesterol - Total.about: The Cholesterol - Total Test test measures the total amount of cholesterol (fats) in the blood. This test helps analyze your overall heart health and monitor the effectiveness of any ongoing cholesterol-lowering treatment. It is a single test, often done as part of the lipid profile test.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of routine health checkups to measure the blood cholesterol level.
To determine an individual's risk of developing heart conditions, stroke, and peripheral artery disease.
To monitor the effectiveness of any ongoing cholesterol-lowering treatment.
To monitor cholesterol levels in individuals with a family history of high cholesterol or premature heart disease.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Cholesterol - HDL.name: Cholesterol - HDL
Cholesterol - HDL.about: The Cholesterol - HDL Test test is a blood test that measures high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels in the body. This test evaluates your cardiovascular health, especially when you have risk factors such as obesity, diabetes, and high blood pressure. It is often done as part of a routine health checkup or lipid profile.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of routine health checkups to measure the HDL cholesterol level in the blood.
To determine an individual's risk of developing heart conditions, stroke, and peripheral artery disease.

For monitoring the HDL levels in individuals already diagnosed with high cholesterol or cardiovascular disease to ensure that their treatment plans are effective in maintaining healthy cholesterol levels.

To detect early deviations in HDL levels in individuals with a family history of high cholesterol levels or premature heart disease, enabling timely interventions and lifestyle modifications to reduce their risk of cardiovascular complications.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

LDL Cholesterol - Direct.name: LDL Cholesterol - Direct
LDL Cholesterol - Direct.about: The LDL Cholesterol - Direct Test test is a blood test that measures the level of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, commonly known as “bad” cholesterol. This test helps assess the risk of heart disease and stroke by providing an accurate measurement of LDL levels in the blood.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To assess the risk of cardiovascular disease
As part of a routine lipid profile check-up
If you have risk factors such as diabetes, obesity, or high blood pressure
To monitor cholesterol-lowering treatment or medications
If you have a family history of cardiovascular disease
To evaluate lipid levels when triglycerides are high

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

Triglycerides.name: Triglycerides
Triglycerides.about: The Triglycerides Test test is a blood test that measures the levels of triglycerides in the body. This test is used to evaluate your risk of developing cardiovascular diseases, especially when you have risk factors, such as obesity, diabetes, and high blood pressure. It is often done as part of a routine health checkup or a lipid profile.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Triglycerides Test test is done:
As part of a routine health checkup to measure the level of triglycerides in the blood.
To evaluate the risk of heart conditions if you have risk factors, such as obesity, diabetes, or a family history of health diseases.
To monitor the treatment response or disease progression in individuals with existing heart disease.
To check the effectiveness of lipid-lowering medicines if you are already on medication for deranged lipids levels.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting (8-12 hrs) is required. Do not eat or drink anything except water before the test.

Lipoprotein (a).name: Lipoprotein (a)
Lipoprotein (a).about: The Lipoprotein (a) Test test measures a specific particle, known as lipoprotein (a), in the blood. It is performed to assess the risk of possible heart diseases such as heart attack and stroke. The test is usually performed in people with a family history of heart disease or in those at high risk for developing heart ailments.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To identify individuals at risk for cardiovascular problems if there is a family history of high Lp-A, heart attack, or stroke.
To assess an individual's risk of developing cardiovascular events such as stroke, coronary artery disease (CAD), or aortic stenosis.
In the case of familial hypercholesterolemia.
In case of recurrent cardiovascular events (like heart attacks and stroke) despite having controlled risk management.
To monitor the effectiveness of treatments in individuals already diagnosed with a heart condition.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Apolipoproteins A1 & B.name: Apolipoproteins A1 & B
Apolipoproteins A1 & B.about: The Apolipoproteins A1 & B test measures the amount of Apolipoprotein A1 and Apolipoprotein B along with Apolipoprotein B/A1 ratio in your blood. This test provides valuable insights into an individual’s heart health by evaluating your risk of developing cardiovascular disease (CVD) such as heart attack, and stroke that can be life-threatening if left untreated.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To identify individuals at risk for developing cardiovascular problems.
In individuals with risk factors like family history, obesity, diabetes, high blood pressure, and prior heart attack or stroke.
When an individual experiences symptoms suggestive of heart disease or cardiovascular problems such as chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, etc.
To help doctors formulate treatment plans according to individual patient needs.

To monitor the effectiveness of ongoing treatments in individuals already diagnosed with heart disease, or to monitor the effect of lifestyle modifications in those identified as “high-risk” individuals for developing future heart-related ailments.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

hsCRP (High Sensitive CRP).name: hsCRP (High Sensitive CRP)
hsCRP (High Sensitive CRP).about: An hsCRP (High Sensitive CRP) Test is a blood test that measures the concentration of C-reactive protein (CRP) in the bloodstream. It derives its name from its greater sensitivity to CRP levels than standard CRP tests. CRP is a marker of inflammation produced by the liver in response to various stimuli, including infection, tissue injury, and inflammation.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: Evaluate your risk of cardiovascular disease or stroke.
Check for bacterial or viral infections if symptoms include fever, chills, redness, swelling, nausea, vomiting, rapid breathing, and/or rapid heart rate.
Detect and monitor the flare-ups of autoimmune diseases, like rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), etc.
Assess the treatment efficacy of chronic inflammatory conditions.
Check for sepsis, a serious life-threatening medical emergency resulting from the body's extreme response to an infection.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

High Sensitive Troponin-I, Quantitative.name: High Sensitive Troponin-I, Quantitative
aka: Risk stratification with cardiac troponin I (cTnI)
High Sensitive Troponin-I, Quantitative.about: The High Sensitive Troponin-I, Quantitative Test test is a highly sensitive blood test used to detect and measure troponin levels, a protein released when the heart muscle is damaged. Cardiac troponins are very specific to the heart muscle and highly sensitive as compared to other older markers of heart damage like creatinine-kinase (CK)-MB, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) enzymes, etc. It helps in the early diagnosis of heart-related conditions, guiding timely medical intervention.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: For the early detection of heart-related problems.
For stratification and risk assessment of heart disease in asymptomatic individuals,
To help in the diagnosis of conditions like Myocardial infarction (heart attack) or other acute coronary syndrome only in emergency settings.
For regular monitoring of individuals with known heart conditions to assess cardiac health and treatment response.
After cardiac procedures to monitor the potential complications and ensure proper recovery.
In emergency situations for rapid insights when an individual presents with symptoms suggestive of cardiac involvement.
For follow-up assessments after cardiac events to guide long-term care strategies.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Creatine Kinase MB.name: Creatine Kinase MB
Creatine Kinase MB.about: The Creatine Kinase MB Test is a blood test that measures the levels of the CK-MB enzyme, which is primarily found in heart muscle cells. This test is crucial for diagnosing heart muscle damage, particularly in conditions like heart attacks, offering valuable insights into overall cardiac health.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To evaluate potential heart damage, particularly in cases of suspected myocardial infarction (heart attack).
To distinguish between skeletal muscle and heart muscle damage.
To detect a second or subsequent heart attack or to monitor for additional heart damage.
To monitor patients with known heart disease or those undergoing treatment for cardiac issues.
To assist in the differential diagnosis of chest pain, distinguishing between cardiac and non-cardiac causes.
To monitor cardiac health after cardiac surgery or procedures.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

NT-Pro BNP.name: NT-Pro BNP
aka: N terminal pro B type natriuretic peptide
NT-Pro BNP.about: The NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide) test is used to measure the levels of NT-proBNP in the blood. NT-proBNP is a hormone produced by the heart in response to increased blood pressure or stress on the heart muscle. It helps diagnose and manage heart-related conditions, such as heart failure.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To diagnose congestive heart failure (CHF) and assess its severity.

If an individual experiences signs and symptoms of heart disease, such as cough, breathlessness, extreme fatigue, swelling in ankles, feet, legs, and veins in the neck, abdominal pain, or frequent urination.
To monitor the response to heart failure treatment.
To differentiate heart failure from other conditions with similar symptoms.
To assess the risk of cardiovascular diseases in individuals with risk factors such as high blood pressure, diabetes, any previous history or family history of heart disease, etc.

prepInfo.title: Patients taking biotin supplements or receiving high-dose biotin therapy are advised to stop supplements for 72 hours before sample collection due to possible interference with this test.

Serum Homocysteine.name: Serum Homocysteine
Serum Homocysteine.about: The Serum Homocysteine Test test determines the levels of homocysteine, a naturally occurring amino acid in your blood. Elevated homocysteine levels may indicate an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, stroke, and other health conditions. High levels of homocysteine are also associated with low levels of vitamins B6, B12, and folate.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To screen for heart attack and stroke, especially in people with no risk factors but with a family history of cardiovascular diseases.
To detect and diagnose an inherited disease called homocystinuria in newborns and infants
To detect deficiencies of Vitamin B6, B12, or B9 (Folic acid).
To identify individuals at higher risk of heart-related issues, even before they develop symptoms.
To monitor the effectiveness of treatments and lifestyle changes in individuals already diagnosed with a heart condition.
To assess overall heart function and as a part of cardiac risk markers.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Advanced Cardiac Risk Markers.name: Advanced Cardiac Risk Markers
Advanced Cardiac Risk Markers.about: An Advanced Cardiac Risk Markers test is a comprehensive blood test that offers detailed information about your risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and the overall health of your heart. Getting tested enables you to make informed health decisions that prevent serious health complications in the future.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To identify individuals at higher risk of heart-related issues, even before they develop symptoms.
To monitor the effectiveness of treatments and lifestyle changes in individuals already diagnosed with a heart condition.
To assess the functioning and overall health of the heart and as part of health checkups.

To determine an individual's risk of developing heart conditions, stroke, and peripheral artery disease, especially those with risk factors such as family history, obesity, diabetes, high blood pressure, and prior heart attack or stroke.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

LFT (Liver Function Test).name: LFT (Liver Function Test)
LFT (Liver Function Test).about: The LFT (Liver Function Test) comprises a group of blood tests measuring the level of various liver enzymes and proteins. It helps assess the liver’s overall health, evaluate and monitor potential liver disease or damage, track the treatment response for known liver problems, and determine if dosage adjustments are needed for medicines that may affect the liver. LFT is often done as part of routine health checkups.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. In Symptomatic Individuals
Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice)
Dark-colored urine
Belly pain
Nausea or vomiting
Chronic fatigue
Loss of appetite
Itchy skin
Unexplained weight loss
B. In High-Risk Individuals (lifestyle, medical conditions, or medication-related risk)
Chronic alcohol consumption
Hepatitis B or C infection
Fatty liver disease or obesity
Use of liver-toxic medications (e.g., certain antibiotics, anti-tuberculosis drugs)
Metabolic disorders such as diabetes or high cholesterol
C. In Special Populations
Individuals with a family history of liver disease
Individuals with known liver issues such as hepatitis, cirrhosis, or liver fibrosis
D. In Individuals Undergoing General Health Checkup
As part of routine health screening
Monitoring disease progression or response to treatment

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

SGPT (Alanine Transaminase).name: SGPT (Alanine Transaminase)
SGPT (Alanine Transaminase).about: An SGPT (Alanine Transaminase) Test test measures the amount of serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase (SGPT) enzyme in the blood. This test helps detect liver diseases, such as jaundice, hepatitis, liver cirrhosis, etc. It may be done as part of a routine health checkup or liver function test to detect possible liver damage or disease.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of a liver function test.
To help detect liver diseases, such as jaundice, liver cirrhosis, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
To monitor an existing liver disease and its treatment response.
To help monitor certain medicines' impact on the liver, such as erythromycin, amiodarone, methyldopa, or amoxicillin-clavulanate.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

SGOT (Aspartate Aminotransferase).name: SGOT (Aspartate Aminotransferase)
SGOT (Aspartate Aminotransferase).about: An SGOT (Aspartate Aminotransferase) Test test measures serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (SGOT) enzyme levels in the blood. This test helps check your liver health and detect underlying diseases like jaundice, hepatitis, etc. It may be done as part of a routine health checkup or liver function test to detect liver damage.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of a liver function test.
To help detect liver diseases, such as jaundice, liver cirrhosis, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
To monitor an existing liver disease and its treatment response.
To help monitor certain medicines' impact on the liver, such as erythromycin, amiodarone, methyldopa, or amoxicillin-clavulanate.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

SGPT & SGOT.name: SGPT & SGOT
SGPT & SGOT.about: The SGPT & SGOT test measures the levels of two important liver enzymes: serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (SGOT) and serum glutamic-pyruvic transaminase (SGPT) in the blood. These tests are commonly done to assess liver function, diagnose liver disorders, and monitor liver health.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To assess liver function and identify potential liver damage or inflammation.
To assess symptoms such as jaundice, abdominal pain, or changes in the color of urine and stool that may indicate potential liver problems.
To help diagnose liver conditions such as hepatitis, cirrhosis, or fatty liver disease.
To screen for liver diseases, especially if you have risk factors such as excessive alcohol use, obesity, or a family history of liver disorders.
To monitor liver function in patients undergoing treatments that might affect the liver.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Bilirubin (Total, Direct and Indirect).name: Bilirubin (Total, Direct and Indirect)
Bilirubin (Total, Direct and Indirect).about: The Bilirubin (Total, Direct and Indirect) Test is a blood test that measures the levels of three different components of bilirubin, including total, direct, and indirect. This test is often done as a part of a liver function test (LFT) to assess liver function and detect possible liver or blood disorders. It helps diagnose and monitor conditions primarily affecting the liver, red blood cells, and bile ducts.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To help diagnose liver diseases, such as jaundice, hepatitis, cirrhosis, etc.
To determine the cause of jaundice (yellowing of the skin and eyes) indicating liver or bile duct problems.
To monitor liver function in individuals with known liver disease or undergoing treatment affecting the liver.
To help diagnose hemolytic anemia, where increased breakdown of red blood cells leads to increased bilirubin levels.
To find out if there is a blockage in the bile duct, such as gallstones or tumors.
In case of risk factors that may affect the liver, such as alcoholism, exposure to hepatitis virus, etc.
To detect and monitor neonatal jaundice.
Often as part of a routine health screening or liver function test (LFT) profile.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP).name: Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP)
Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP).about: An Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) Test test measures the amount of ALP enzyme in the body. This test helps detect liver diseases, such as hepatitis, liver cirrhosis, and bile duct obstruction. It is done as part of routine health checkups or a liver function test to detect any liver damage.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of a liver function test.
To monitor an existing liver disease and its treatment response.
To detect bile duct stricture and obstruction.
To detect a bone disease if you have signs and symptoms like bone pain and increased frequency of fractures.
To diagnose cholestasis of pregnancy.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Gamma Glutamyl Transferase.name: Gamma Glutamyl Transferase
Gamma Glutamyl Transferase.about: The Gamma Glutamyl Transferase Test measures the amount of Gamma Glutamyl Transferase (GGT), a liver enzyme, in the body. This test is used to check for any blockage in the bile ducts and monitor the treatment response of liver diseases such as jaundice and hepatitis.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of a liver function test.
To monitor an existing liver disease and its treatment response.
To detect diseases associated with bile duct obstruction.
When alkaline phosphatase (ALP) enzyme levels are elevated.
To figure out if liver damage is due to a liver disease or bone disorder.
To monitor alcohol use disorder.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Serum Albumin.name: Serum Albumin
Serum Albumin.about: The Serum Albumin Test test measures the amount of albumin protein in the body. This test helps determine your nutritional status or identify any nutritional deficiencies. It is recommended as part of routine health checkups or if a liver or kidney disease is suspected.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of routine health checkups.
If you have symptoms of liver or kidney disease.
To monitor treatment response for existing liver and kidney diseases.
In case of a planned surgery.
In case of sudden weight loss.
To check the nutritional status.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Protein Total, Serum.name: Protein Total, Serum
Protein Total, Serum.about: The Protein Total, Serum Test test measures the levels of different proteins in the blood. This test helps assess liver and kidney health along with detecting any underlying problems associated with these organs. It may also help determine your nutritional status and detect any nutritional deficiencies.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of routine health checkups.
To detect liver and kidney diseases.
To monitor liver and kidney health if you are taking medications that can affect these organs.
In case of unexpected weight loss or fatigue.
To check nutritional status.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg).name: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg)
Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg).about: The Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) test detects the presence of the hepatitis B virus (HBV) in the body. It helps detects the hepatitis B surface antigen in the blood, indicating an active infection. This test is crucial for early diagnosis, treatment planning, and supports prevention measures for hepatitis B.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. Screening Purposes
To check for hepatitis B infection in high-risk individuals
For blood donation or pre-surgical evaluations
For routine health checkups
B. Confirming Diagnosis
To detect acute or chronic hepatitis B infection
To differentiate hepatitis B from other liver diseases when interpreted alongside other hepatitis B markers
C. Monitoring and Follow-Up
To monitor the effectiveness of hepatitis B treatment along with other hepatitis B tests
To check for chronic carrier status in previously infected individuals

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Antibody.name: Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Antibody
Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Antibody.about: The Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Antibody test is used to detect antibodies to the hepatitis C virus (HCV) in blood.
