This test plays a crucial role in screening of HCV infection. It helps determine whether an individual has a current, recent (acute) or past hepatitis C infection and monitor treatment response.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To screen for hepatitis C infection if you have been exposed to HCV or show symptoms associated with liver disease.
To screen for hepatitis C infection if you have risk factors for developing an HCV infection.
To screen individuals at high risk of Hepatitis C infection, such as individuals who inject drugs, those with a history of unsafe medical procedures, or individuals born to mothers with hepatitis C.
To identify hepatitis C infection early for timely intervention, reducing the risk of long-term liver damage.
For antiviral treatment guidance.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Hepatitis A Antibody, IgG + IgM.name: Hepatitis A Antibody, IgG + IgM
Hepatitis A Antibody, IgG + IgM.about: The Hepatitis A Antibody, IgG + IgM test helps detect immunoglobulin M (IgM) and immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies in the blood against Hepatitis A virus (HAV). It helps diagnose current or acute infection (indicated by IgM) or past infection or vaccination, showing long-term immunity (indicated by IgG), helping in timely and effective management.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To detect acute or recent infection with the hepatitis A virus (HAV).
To confirm past exposure to the hepatitis A virus (HAV) or immunity due to vaccination.
To differentiate between infection types by distinguishing a recent HAV infection (indicated by IgM) from long-term immunity (indicated by IgG).
When there are symptoms such as abdominal pain, fatigue, jaundice, etc., suggestive of a liver disease.
To evaluate your risk of developing hepatitis A infection, especially in high-risk populations such as healthcare workers or travel history to areas where the virus is prevalent.
To monitor at-risk populations, including pregnant women, healthcare workers, or travelers to endemic regions.
To determine the need for further vaccination or booster doses.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Hepatitis E Virus, IgM Antibody.name: Hepatitis E Virus, IgM Antibody
Hepatitis E Virus, IgM Antibody.about: The Hepatitis E Virus, IgM Antibody is a blood test that detects Immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibodies produced by the immune system in response to the recent (acute) Hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection. It helps diagnose Hepatitis E and assess whether an individual has immunity to this disease.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To detect acute or recent infection with the Hepatitis E virus (HEV).
When there are symptoms such as abdominal pain, fatigue, jaundice etc., suggestive of a liver disease.
To confirm the exposure to HEV, especially in individuals with known contact with contaminated food and water.
To diagnose HEV infection in pregnant women, immunocompromised individuals, young children and travelers to endemic areas.
To monitor the spread of HEV within a community or outbreak settings.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

BUN-Urea-Creatinine.name: BUN-Urea-Creatinine
BUN-Urea-Creatinine.about: The BUN-Urea-Creatinine test comprises a group of blood tests that help assess the overall health of the kidneys and their ability to filter waste products from the blood. This test is commonly done as a part of the kidney function test (KFT) to evaluate kidney function, diagnose kidney disorders, and monitor the progression of kidney diseases.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of routine health checkups.
If you have signs and symptoms that indicate kidney dysfunction such as urinary changes, stomach pain, muscle cramps, loss of appetite, and fatigue.
To screen for kidney diseases if you have risk factors like obesity, diabetes, high blood pressure, or a family history of kidney disease.
To monitor kidney function in patients undergoing treatments that can affect the health of kidneys.
To help determine the effectiveness of dialysis or other ongoing treatments for kidney disease.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Serum Creatinine.name: Serum Creatinine
Serum Creatinine.about: The Serum Creatinine Test measures the levels of creatinine, a waste product produced by muscles during energy metabolism, in the blood. This test is an important indicator of kidney function and overall health. It is commonly done as part of a kidney function test (KFT) or routine check-up.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Serum Creatinine Test is done:
A. In Symptomatic Individuals
Swelling in the hands, feet, or ankles
Fatigue or generalized weakness
Decreased urine output or changes in urination patterns
Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Nausea or vomiting
Confusion or difficulty concentrating
Muscle cramps
B. In High-Risk Groups
Chronic kidney disease (CKD)
History of kidney problems
Hypertension (high blood pressure) or cardiovascular disease
Diabetes
Obesity
Taking medications that can affect kidney function (e.g., NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors)
C. In Special Populations
Elderly individuals
People with a family history of kidney disease
D. In Individuals with Known Kidney Issues
Previously abnormal kidney function tests (KFT)
A confirmed diagnosis of chronic kidney disease (CKD)
E. As Part Of the Kidney Function Test (KFT)
Routine monitoring of kidney function

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Creatinine with eGFR (18 Years & Above).name: Creatinine with eGFR (18 Years & Above)
aka: Serum creatinine with estimated glomerular filtration rate
Creatinine with eGFR (18 Years & Above).about: In this test, serum creatinine is measured in the blood, and the glomerular filtration rate is estimated using the 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equation for estimating GFR in adults (above 18 years). The eGFR is a calculation used to estimate how well your kidneys are filtering waste produced by your body. It is used to estimate kidney function especially in people who are at higher risk of developing kidney disease. This test is done in people who suffer from chronic kidney disease(CKD), hypertension,obesity, and diabetes.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To evaluate kidney function and detect any disease or disorder of the kidneys.
If you have risk factors like obesity, diabetes, high blood pressure, or a family history of kidney disease.
To monitor treatment response of kidney disease.
To determine drug dosages and monitor potential kidney toxicity that may be caused by certain medications.
To evaluate baseline kidney function before surgeries or medical procedures.

prepInfo.title: Patient's age and gender are mandatory. This test is applicable for patients aged 18 years or more.

Blood Urea.name: Blood Urea
Blood Urea.about: The Blood Urea Test test measures the level of urea in the blood. This test is done to detect any kidney disease or damage, or if you are undergoing treatment for an already existing kidney disease. This test is performed as part of a routine health checkup to determine your kidney function.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of routine health checkups.
In the case of signs and symptoms of kidney disease.
To screen for kidney disease if you have risk factors like obesity, diabetes, high blood pressure, or a family history of kidney disease.
To check the effectiveness of undergoing treatment for kidney diseases.
To help determine the effectiveness of dialysis if someone is receiving hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Blood Urea Nitrogen.name: Blood Urea Nitrogen
Blood Urea Nitrogen.about: The Blood Urea Nitrogen Test measures the level of urea nitrogen in the blood. This test is done to detect any kidney disease or damage, or if you are undergoing treatment for any known kidney disease. It is often done as part of routine health checkups to determine your kidney function.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Blood Urea Nitrogen Test is done:
As part of routine health checkups.
In the case of signs and symptoms of kidney disease.
To screen for kidney disease if you have risk factors like obesity, diabetes, high blood pressure, or a family history of kidney disease.
To check for the effectiveness of ongoing treatment for kidney diseases.
To help determine the effectiveness of dialysis treatment if someone is receiving hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Uric Acid, Serum.name: Uric Acid, Serum
Uric Acid, Serum.about: The Uric Acid, Serum Test measures the levels of uric acid, a natural waste product formed from the breakdown of purines (found in certain foods and body tissues). This test is important for assessing kidney function and metabolic balance and is commonly done as part of a routine health checkup or along with a kidney function test (KFT).

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. In Symptomatic Individuals:
Sudden severe joint pain or swelling (commonly in the big toe)
Redness or warmth around joints
Pain or difficulty in moving affected joints
Signs of kidney stones, such as back pain or blood in urine
Unexplained fatigue, generalized weakness, or metabolic disturbances
B. In High-Risk Groups:
Obesity
High blood pressure or cardiovascular disease
Diabetes or metabolic syndrome
Family history of gout or kidney disease
Taking medications that can affect uric acid levels (e.g., diuretics, chemotherapy drugs, aspirin)
C. In Special Populations:
Elderly individuals
Individuals with a family history of gout, kidney stones, or hyperuricemia
D. In Individuals with Known Metabolic or Kidney Issues:
Previously abnormal uric acid test results
History of kidney stones
Monitoring during treatment for gout or other metabolic conditions

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Serum Electrolytes.name: Serum Electrolytes
Serum Electrolytes.about: The Serum Electrolytes Test test measures the levels of three important electrolytes: sodium, potassium, and chloride in the body. This test evaluates your overall health and detects or monitors issues with the kidneys, nerves, or heart. It may be done as part of routine health checkups or if someone experiences symptoms of electrolyte imbalance.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Serum Electrolytes Test test is done:
As part of routine health checkups.
If you experience symptoms suggestive of electrolyte imbalance, such as weakness, fatigue, muscle cramps, or changes in heart rate.
To monitor kidney, heart, or chronic illnesses.
To check if medicines like diuretics are affecting your electrolytes.
During or after IV fluid treatment or dialysis.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Sodium.name: Sodium
Sodium.about: The Sodium Test test measures the amount of sodium, an electrolyte, in your body. This test evaluates your overall health and may be done as a follow-up test for conditions like high blood pressure or as part of a routine health checkup.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Sodium Test test is done:
As part of routine health checkups.
To check your body's water-electrolyte balance and acid-base (pH) balance.
To detect the cause and monitor the treatment of dehydration or excess fluid buildup (edema).
To monitor the progress of the condition and treatment response while undergoing treatment for high blood pressure and diseases related to the kidneys, heart, liver, or adrenal gland.
To monitor patients receiving diuretic therapy, intravenous fluids, or dialysis.
To check the effects of medications that can affect your sodium levels, such as diuretics, birth control pills, antidepressants, and opioids.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Potassium.name: Potassium
Potassium.about: The Potassium Test measures the amount of potassium, an important electrolyte, in your body. This test is performed to evaluate your overall health. It can also be used as a follow-up test for ongoing health conditions like high blood pressure, kidney disease, heart problems, etc. This test is done as part of a routine health checkup.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Potassium Test is done:
As part of routine health checkups.
To detect kidney-related health problems.
To monitor acid-base (pH) balance in the body.
To detect abnormalities if you experience symptoms such as muscular weakness, irregular heartbeats, or cardiac arrhythmia.
To monitor the progress of the condition and treatment response while undergoing treatment for high blood pressure, heart disease, kidney diseases, metabolic acidosis, and diabetes.
To monitor patients who are receiving diuretic therapy, intravenous fluids, or dialysis.

To check the effects of medicines that can potentially affect your potassium levels, such as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), corticosteroids, antifungal medicines, beta-blockers, ACE enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs), and diuretics.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Chloride.name: Chloride
Chloride.about: The Chloride Test test measures the levels of chloride, an important electrolyte, in your body. This test is performed to evaluate your overall health or as a follow-up test for ongoing conditions like high blood pressure or problems related to the kidneys, liver, or heart. This test is often done as part of a routine health checkup.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Chloride Test test is done:
As part of routine health checkups.
To check the water and electrolyte balance in the body.
To check the acid-base (pH) balance of the body.
To monitor the progress of the condition and treatment response while undergoing treatment for high blood pressure and diseases related to the kidneys, heart, or liver.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Cystatin C.name: Cystatin C
Cystatin C.about: The Cystatin C Test is a blood test that measures the level of cystatin C, a protein produced by all body cells and excreted by the kidneys. This test helps doctors see how well your kidneys are working, especially if other tests like creatinine are unreliable.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To assess how well your kidneys are functioning.
As an early detection marker for kidney disease
To identify kidney problems in individuals with risks like obesity, diabetes, or family history.
To keep track of kidney health in individuals who already have kidney issues or are getting treatment.
To give a more accurate result when other tests, like creatinine, might not be reliable.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Protein/Creatinine Ratio.name: Protein/Creatinine Ratio
Protein/Creatinine Ratio.about: The Protein/Creatinine Ratio Test test helps calculate the amount of protein relative to creatinine in a urine sample. It helps screen, assess, and monitor kidney function. It helps in the diagnosis of kidney damage or diseases, among several other conditions that can affect kidney health.

sampleInfo.title: Urine
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will provide a clean, sterile container for you to collect a urine sample.

why.title: To help detect and monitor kidney dysfunction or disease early on by measuring the amount of protein in the urine, a sensitive indicator of kidney problem.
To assess the amount of excessive protein in the urine (proteinuria), an indicator of kidney dysfunction.
To monitor chronic conditions like diabetes and hypertension, which can lead to kidney damage over time.
To monitor treatment response against kidney diseases.
To screen for pre-eclampsia (a condition characterized by high blood pressure and protein in the urine) in pregnant women.
To evaluate children with high urine protein levels.

prepInfo.title: Collect a Random/Spot urine sample (a minimum quantity of 10 ml urine) in a sealed and sterile screw-capped container provided by our sample collection professional. Women are advised not to give the sample during the menstrual period unless prescribed. Blood contaminated and highly turbid samples are not acceptable.

Kidney Health Screen.name: Kidney Health Screen
Kidney Health Screen.about: The Kidney Health Screen is a comprehensive assessment tailored to evaluate kidney function and detect potential issues early. It includes a range of blood and urine tests that provide a holistic view of kidney health, helping in the early detection and management of kidney-related conditions.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

sampleInfo.title: Urine
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will provide a clean, sterile container for you to collect a urine sample.

why.title: As part of routine health evaluations for overall well-being.
If you have signs and symptoms that indicate kidney dysfunction such as changes in urine output, swelling, fatigue, stomach pain, muscle cramps, loss of appetite etc.
To screen for kidney diseases if you have risk factors like obesity, diabetes, high blood pressure, or a family history of kidney disease.
To monitor kidney function in patients undergoing treatments that can affect the health of kidneys.
To help determine the effectiveness of dialysis or other ongoing treatments for kidney disease.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

The urine sample (a minimum quantity of 10 ml urine) must preferably be the first morning midstream urine (part of urine that comes after the first and before the last stream). Collect the urine sample in a sealed and sterile screw-capped container provided by our sample collection professional. Ensure that the urethral area (from where the urine is passed) is clean & container doesn't come in contact with your skin. Women are advised not to give the sample during the menstrual period unless prescribed. You should submit all the required samples for this package at once during the scheduled sample collection.

Stone Analysis, Kidney calculus.name: Stone Analysis, Kidney calculus
aka: Calculus (Stone) Analysis by automated FTIR (Kidney (Renal) calculus)
Stone Analysis, Kidney calculus.about: The Stone Analysis, Kidney calculus test examines the kidney stones (hard deposits made from minerals and salts) for their structure, composition, and other characteristics. The test helps understand why they formed in the kidneys and what the stone is made of, such as calcium, uric acid, or other materials.

why.title: When an individual is experiencing symptoms like severe pain, blood in the urine, frequent urination, or painful urination.
When someone has previously had kidney stones and is at risk of forming new ones.
After a kidney stone has been passed or surgically removed to identify its composition.
To determine the exact chemical makeup of the kidney stone (e.g., calcium oxalate, uric acid, struvite).
To tailor treatment plans based on the type of stone, as different types require different treatments.
To evaluate how well current treatment methods are working and if adjustments are needed.
To help prevent future stone formation by understanding the mineral composition and advising on lifestyle changes or medications.

prepInfo.title: Clinical history is preferred.

Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy).name: Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy)
Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy).about: The Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy) measures the level of 25-hydroxy vitamin D in the body. Vitamin D helps your body to absorb calcium and phosphorus, which are important for strong bones and teeth. It also supports your immune system. This test helps you assess bone health and immunity.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy) can be done:
A. In Symptomatic Individuals
Bone or joint pain
Chronic fatigue
Muscle weakness or cramps
Susceptibility to frequent infections
B. In High-Risk Groups
Osteoporosis or other bone disorders
Inflammatory bowel disease
Malabsorption syndromes (e.g., celiac disease, Crohn’s disease)
Chronic kidney or liver diseases
C. In Special Populations
Pregnant and lactating women
Elderly individuals
Infants receiving exclusive breastfeeding
D. In Individuals With Lifestyle-Related Risks
Limited sun exposure
Strict vegan diet
Obesity

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Vitamin B12.name: Vitamin B12
Vitamin B12.about: The Vitamin B12 Test measures the level of vitamin B12 in the blood. This vitamin is vital for brain health, nerve function, energy production, and red blood cell formation. Deficiency of vitamin B12 can cause a range of health problems, including tiredness, anemia, neurological problems, tingling in hands and feet, etc.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. In Symptomatic Individuals
Numbness
Muscle weakness
Rapid breathing or shortness of breath
Blurred vision due to anemia or nerve-related issues
B. In High-Risk Groups
Medical conditions affecting vitamin B12 absorption (such as Crohn’s disease and gastrectomy)
Anemia
C. In Special Population
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Elderly
D. Lifestyle-Related Risks
A vegan or vegetarian diet
Chronic alcohol consumption

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Vitamin B9 (Folic Acid).name: Vitamin B9 (Folic Acid)
Vitamin B9 (Folic Acid).about: The Vitamin B9 (Folic Acid) Test measures the level of vitamin B9 in the body. This vitamin is vital for forming red blood cells, DNA synthesis, and the growth of cells and other body tissues. Its deficiency may cause anemia and symptoms like weakness, confusion, breathing issues, etc.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of a routine checkup to monitor your overall health.
As a monitoring parameter for a healthy pregnancy.
If you have symptoms of low vitamin B9 levels, such as weakness, fatigue, mouth ulcers, reduced sense of taste, memory loss, etc.
If you have been diagnosed with folate-deficiency anemia.
If you are on medications that may interfere with the absorption of vitamin 9.
If the doctor suspects a medical condition that affects vitamin B9 absorption in your body.
To evaluate your nutritional status (poor diet or malnutrition).
To monitor the treatment for vitamin B9 deficiency.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy) & Vitamin B12.name: Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy) & Vitamin B12
Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy) & Vitamin B12.about: The Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy) & Vitamin B12 test measures the level of vitamin D and vitamin B12 in your body. This test helps determine deficiencies related to vitamin D and B12. It also helps assess if you have too much of these vitamins in your body (most likely from excessive supplements). Vitamin D helps keep bones, teeth, and muscles healthy, whereas vitamin B12 maintains blood, brain, and nerve functions.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. In Symptomatic Individuals
Chronic fatigue
Muscle weakness or cramps
Numbness or tingling
Bone or joint pain
Rapid breathing or shortness of breath
Blurred vision
Susceptibility to frequent infections
B. In health-specific conditions
Osteoporosis
Inflammatory bowel diseases (e.g., Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis)
Malabsorption syndromes (e.g., celiac disease)
Chronic kidney or liver disease
History of gastrectomy or other gastrointestinal surgery
Anemia (especially megaloblastic anemia)
C. In Special Populations
Pregnant or breastfeeding women
Elderly individuals
Infants who are exclusively breastfed
D. In Individuals With Lifestyle-Related Risks
Limited sun exposure (risk for Vitamin D deficiency)
Strict vegan or vegetarian diet (risk for Vitamin B12 deficiency)
Obesity
Chronic alcohol consumption

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Vitamin D, B12 & Calcium.name: Vitamin D, B12 & Calcium
Vitamin D, B12 & Calcium.about: The Vitamin D, B12 & Calcium test measures the levels of vitamin D (25-Hydroxy), vitamin B12, and calcium in the blood. These tests are essential for evaluating bone strength, nerve function, and overall health. These tests help detect deficiencies or excesses that could lead to health problems.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To assess bone health and immune function and detect deficiencies or excesses affecting overall well-being.
To check for deficiencies impacting energy levels, red blood cell production, or nerve function.
To monitor bone strength, muscle function, and overall mineral balance and identify imbalances that can lead to health issues.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

Vitamin Profile.name: Vitamin Profile
Vitamin Profile.about: The Vitamin Profile is a group of tests that assesses the levels of vitamin B12 (cobalamin), vitamin D, and vitamin B9 (folate) in the body. These tests help check overall health, find any vitamin deficiency, and see if the diet or supplements are effective.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To check if the body has enough Vitamin B9, B12, and D.
To find out if you have a vitamin deficiency.
To understand the cause of symptoms like tiredness, weakness, or mood changes.
To help diagnose health problems like anemia, bone weakness, or nerve issues.
To monitor your vitamin levels if you're taking supplements or changing your diet.
To support overall health, especially during pregnancy, old age, or chronic illness.
To help prevent long-term problems like osteoporosis or immune system disorders.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Vitamin B Complex Profile.name: Vitamin B Complex Profile
Vitamin B Complex Profile.about: The Vitamin B Complex Profile helps determine the levels of different types of vitamin B like B1, B2, B6, B9, and B12 in the body. It helps detect potential vitamin B deficiencies. It can be done as a part of a routine checkup especially if there are symptoms or risks associated with a deficiency.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of a routine checkup to monitor your overall health.
To check the levels of essential vitamins, including vitamins B1, B2, B6, B9 and B12.
If you experience symptoms such as fatigue, general weakness, numbness or tingling in hands and feet, weakened muscles, skin rash, cracked lips, mood swings, etc suggestive of a vitamin B deficiency.
If you are suffering from chronic conditions like diabetes, high cholesterol, obesity, etc.
If you have been previously diagnosed with folate-deficiency anemia, megaloblastic anemia, pernicious anemia, or microcytic anemia.
As a monitoring parameter for a healthy pregnancy in pregnant women.
If you are on medications that may interfere with vitamin B absorption.
If your doctor suspects a medical condition that affects vitamin B absorption in your body.
To evaluate the nutritional status and determine if there is a need for dietary adjustments or supplementation to maintain optimal health.

Vitamin E - Quantitative.name: Vitamin E - Quantitative
Vitamin E - Quantitative.about: The Vitamin E - Quantitative Test test is a blood test that helps determine the levels of vitamin E in the body, a strong antioxidant that protects cells from free radicals. It helps detect potential vitamin E deficiencies or toxicity, which can have significant health consequences.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Vitamin E - Quantitative Test test is done:
To check the levels of vitamin E in the body.
If there are symptoms like weak muscles, vision problems, trouble walking, or poor coordination, indicating a vitamin E deficiency.
If someone has health problems that make it hard to absorb fat, like cystic fibrosis, Crohn’s disease, or liver disease.
To check if vitamin E supplements are working effectively or to check vitamin E toxicity.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Serum Calcium.name: Serum Calcium
Serum Calcium.about: The Serum Calcium Test measures the calcium level in your blood. Calcium is an essential mineral. It helps build strong bones and teeth. It also controls muscle movement, nerve function, heart rhythm, and blood clotting. This test checks your overall calcium balance. It helps monitor your bone, kidney, or parathyroid health.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. In Symptomatic Individuals
Muscle cramps or twitching
Tingling or numbness in the extremities
Bone pain or tenderness
Irregular heartbeat
B. In High-Risk Groups
Individuals with kidney disease
Individuals with suspected parathyroid gland problems
Individuals with vitamin D deficiency
C. In Special Populations
Pregnant women (to monitor calcium balance)
Elderly individuals (risk of bone loss and osteoporosis)
Patients on prolonged medications affecting calcium metabolism
D. In Individuals With Lifestyle-Related Risks
Excessive consumption of calcium or vitamin D supplements
Sedentary lifestyle or limited sun exposure

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

Calcium Ionized.name: Calcium Ionized
Calcium Ionized.about: The calcium ionized blood test measures only the free (unattached to proteins), active form of calcium. It provides a more precise assessment of calcium status and helps diagnose and monitor conditions like parathyroid disorders, kidney disease, and bone and intestinal diseases. It helps ensure that your body has the right amount of calcium to function properly.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To evaluate calcium metabolism and detect imbalances in calcium levels.
To help diagnose conditions affecting the parathyroid glands, such as hyperparathyroidism or hypoparathyroidism.
To monitor kidney function and detect abnormalities related to calcium excretion.
To assess bone health and the risk of osteoporosis or other bone diseases.
To assess calcium levels during any procedure requiring rapid transfusion.
To evaluate body’s acid -base balance and detect conditions like acidosis or alkalosis.
To monitor the effectiveness of treatments that affect calcium levels, such as calcium medications for bone disorders.
To investigate the cause of symptoms such as muscle spasms, numbness, or irregular heartbeat that might be associated with calcium imbalances

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

Magnesium.name: Magnesium
Magnesium.about: The Magnesium Test is used to determine the level of magnesium, a vital mineral, in blood. It is done to evaluate kidney problems or uncontrolled diabetes. It may also be performed to help diagnose gastrointestinal (relating to the stomach and intestines) disorders.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Magnesium Test is done:
As part of a routine health checkup.
If symptoms of magnesium deficiency appear (e.g., muscle cramps, irregular heartbeat, seizures).
When calcium or potassium test results are abnormal.
To evaluate conditions like kidney disease, gastrointestinal issues, uncontrolled diabetes, or alcoholism.
In pregnancy, especially when checking for signs of preeclampsia.
To monitor the effect of magnesium supplements.If symptoms of magnesium deficiency appear (e.g., muscle cramps, irregular heartbeat, seizures).

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Phosphorus, Serum.name: Phosphorus, Serum
Phosphorus, Serum.about: The Phosphorus, Serum Test test measures the amount of phosphorus, an important mineral in your body. The test is done to evaluate phosphate levels in case of bone and kidney disease, to determine the cause of the abnormal level of vitamin D, and to monitor the effectiveness of phosphorus and calcium supplementation.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Phosphorus, Serum Test test is done:
To evaluate phosphate levels in case of bone and kidney diseases.
To determine conditions associated with certain glands like parathyroid glands.
To determine the cause of abnormal levels of vitamin D.
In case of uncontrolled diabetes.
To monitor treatment effectiveness when taking phosphorus or calcium supplements.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

Zinc, Serum.name: Zinc, Serum
Zinc, Serum.about: A Zinc, Serum Test test helps to determine the levels of zinc in your body, an essential mineral that contributes significantly to various bodily functions, including immune system support, wound healing, and metabolism. This test helps identify deficiencies or excesses of the zinc ensuring the optimal presence of this element necessary for overall well-being.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To assess zinc levels in the body.
To identify zinc deficiencies or excesses of zinc.
To evaluate nutritional health.
To detect conditions associated with zinc imbalance.
To monitor and address symptoms related to low or high zinc levels.
To monitor treatment for zinc deficiency.
In pregnant women to determine the level of zinc.

prepInfo.title: Avoid taking zinc tablets for at least 24 hours before sample collection.

Copper Serum.name: Copper Serum
Copper Serum.about: The Copper Serum Test measures the amount of copper in the blood. Copper is an essential mineral that supports red blood cell production, collagen formation, energy generation, and the proper functioning of the nervous and immune systems. This test helps support the diagnosis and monitoring of conditions related to copper metabolism, nutritional imbalances, and certain liver or neurological disorders.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: Diagnose and monitor disorders of copper metabolism, such as Wilson’s disease or Menkes disease.
Identify nutritional imbalances, including copper deficiency or excess.
Track the effectiveness of treatment in patients with copper-related conditions.
Evaluate liver function and overall health, since the liver plays a major role in copper storage and regulation.
When you have symptoms or a family history of Wilson’s disease or Menkes disease.

prepInfo.title: Patient should avoid eating herbal supplements for 3 days prior to sample collection. The test should not be taken for 96 hours if Gadolinium or Iodine containing contrast media used for imaging.

Serum Prolactin.name: Serum Prolactin
Serum Prolactin.about: The Serum Prolactin Test test checks the amount of prolactin, a hormone made by the pituitary gland. This hormone plays a role in various body functions. In women, prolactin supports breast growth and milk production during pregnancy and breastfeeding. In men, it helps control immune function and supports reproductive health.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: Check for infertility, irregular periods, or abnormal milk discharge (galactorrhea) in non-pregnant women.
To find out why a woman may not be producing milk after childbirth.
Investigate erection problems or breast discharge in men.
Assess low sex drive in both men and women.
Detect and monitors prolactinomas (non-cancerous tumors) in the pituitary gland.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory.
A morning sample (preferably collected 2–3 hours after waking) is recommended.
Follow your doctor's instructions regarding the timing of the test and any fasting requirements.

LH & FSH.name: LH & FSH
LH & FSH.about: The LH & FSH Test test helps assess the levels of two vital hormones: follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) in both males and females. These hormones play an important role in reproductive health, with Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing Hormone (LH) regulating the menstrual cycle in females and sperm production in males. This test is performed to detect and monitor hormonal imbalance, infertility issues and early or delayed puberty.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To evaluate the function of reproductive organs (ovaries or testicles).
To assess menstrual irregularities and conditions such as amenorrhea or oligomenorrhea in females
To detect disorders of the pituitary gland or diseases involving the ovaries in females
To investigate fertility problems in both males and females.
To evaluate low sperm count in males.
To assess hypogonadism or gonadal failure in males.
To assess testicular dysfunction in men.
To evaluate early or delayed sexual maturation (puberty) in children.
To investigate and monitor conditions affecting sexual development and puberty in both males and females.
To monitor hormone levels during hormone replacement therapy (HRT).

prepInfo.title: In females, the preferred sampling time is day 2 or 3 of the menstrual cycle for LH & FSH.

Luteinising Hormone.name: Luteinising Hormone
Luteinising Hormone.about: The Luteinising Hormone Test test measures the amount of luteinizing hormone (LH) in your blood. LH is vital in maintaining a healthy reproductive system in both men and women. This test is performed to evaluate the health of the reproductive organs, irregularities in menstrual cycles, fertility issues, and early or late puberty.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: Evaluate the function of reproductive organs (ovaries or testicles).
Assess menstrual irregularities and conditions such as amenorrhea or oligomenorrhea.
Detects disorders of the pituitary gland or diseases involving the ovaries.
Evaluate infertility issues in men and women.
Evaluate low sperm count in men.
Assess hypogonadism or gonadal failure in men.
Assess testicular dysfunction in men.
Evaluate early or delayed sexual maturation (puberty) in children.

prepInfo.title: In females, the preferred sampling time is day 2 or 3 of the menstrual cycle for LH & FSH.

Follicle Stimulating Hormone.name: Follicle Stimulating Hormone
Follicle Stimulating Hormone.about: The Follicle Stimulating Hormone test measures the level of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH). FSH is a hormone that plays a significant role in sexual development and reproduction in men and women. This test is performed to detect and monitor hormonal imbalance, fertility issues and early or delayed puberty.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Follicle Stimulating Hormone test is done to:
Evaluate the function of reproductive organs (ovaries or testicles).
Assess menstrual irregularities and conditions such as amenorrhea or oligomenorrhea.
Detects disorders of the pituitary gland or diseases involving the ovaries.
Evaluate infertility issues in men and women.
Evaluate low sperm count in men.
Assess hypogonadism or gonadal failure in men.
Assess testicular dysfunction in men.
Evaluate early or delayed sexual maturation (puberty) in children.

prepInfo.title: In females, the preferred sampling time is day 2 or 3 of the menstrual cycle for LH & FSH.

FSH, LH & Prolactin.name: FSH, LH & Prolactin
FSH, LH & Prolactin.about: The Hormonal Profile includes three important hormones: Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH), Luteinizing Hormone (LH), and Prolactin. These hormones help control reproductive functions and milk production. This test helps in identifying and managing hormonal issues and fertility problems.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: Check fertility issues in men and women.
Investigate irregular or absent periods (amenorrhea or oligomenorrhea).
Find the cause of unusual breast milk discharge (galactorrhea) in women who are not pregnant.
Understand low milk production in women after delivery.
Diagnose problems or tumors in the pituitary gland, or diseases affecting the ovaries or testicles.

prepInfo.title: In females, the preferred sampling time is day 2 or 3 of the menstrual cycle for LH & FSH.
Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.
For Prolactin- A morning sample (preferably collected 2–3 hours after waking) is recommended. Kindly follow your doctor's instructions, if any, on how to prepare for your test.

AMH (Anti-Mullerian Hormone).name: AMH (Anti-Mullerian Hormone)
AMH (Anti-Mullerian Hormone).about: The AMH (Anti-Mullerian Hormone) Test measures the level of anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) in your body. AMH is produced in both males and females and serves as a marker of reproductive function. In women, it is primarily used to assess ovarian reserve, while in men, it serves as a marker of Sertoli cell function and may aid in the evaluation of testicular function.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: In Symptomatic Individuals
Irregular or missed menstrual cycles
Difficulty conceiving or unexplained infertility
Early signs of menopause
Hot flashes
Abnormal testicular development or delayed puberty in males
In High-Risk Groups
Diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
Early menopause
History of ovarian surgery or cancer treatments (e.g., chemotherapy, radiation)
History of testicular disorders or treatments that may affect testicular function
In Special Populations
Women planning to delay pregnancy
Women considering egg freezing or IVF
For the testicular function in men
Infants with ambiguous genitalia and other intersex conditions
Children being evaluated for delayed or abnormal puberty
Selected adult males undergoing evaluation for testicular or reproductive disorders

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.
If you take hormonal birth control pills, consult your doctor as they can interfere with the results.

E2 (Estradiol).name: E2 (Estradiol)
E2 (Estradiol).about: An E2 (Estradiol) test measures the amount of estradiol, a form of estrogen hormone, in the blood. This test is used to assess reproductive health, diagnose hormone-related conditions, monitor fertility treatments, and evaluate certain health conditions such as menstrual irregularities, infertility, and menopausal symptoms.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: Evaluate ovarian function, menstrual irregularities, and menopausal status.
Monitor the health of the placenta during pregnancy.
Diagnose hormonal disorders, including PCOS, hypogonadism, hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, and adrenal gland disorders.
Assess puberty development in males and females.
Monitor treatment response in women taking hormone replacement therapy after menopause.
Evaluate ovarian follicle development, predict response to fertility treatments such as in vitro fertilization (IVF), and monitor fertility treatment protocols.
Evaluate the lack of secondary sexual features, muscle mass, and causes of gynecomastia (enlarged breasts) in men.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Progesterone.name: Progesterone
Progesterone.about: A Progesterone Test test is a blood test that evaluates the levels of progesterone, a key hormone important for various aspects of reproductive health. This test is often done to understand reproductive health, support fertility evaluation, and address hormonal imbalances that may affect menstrual cycles and pregnancy in females.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To determine the cause of infertility
To track ovulation
To investigate the cause of irregularities in menstrual cycles
To identify potential issue with ovarian function
To monitor the progression of a pregnancy
To help diagnose an ectopic or failing pregnancy
To monitor a high-risk pregnancy
To check whether you’re at high risk of miscarriage during pregnancy
To assess the luteal phase deficiency (LPD)
To diagnose the cause of abnormal uterine bleeding
For women undergoing hormone therapy

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.
Specify age, sex, last menstrual period (LMP) and menopausal status on test request form for sample collection.

Testosterone Total.name: Testosterone Total
Testosterone Total.about: The Testosterone Total Test test is a blood test that measures the amount of testosterone. It is primarily a male sex hormone, but found in both men and women. This test helps determine hormonal balance and detects conditions like low testosterone, infertility, or hormonal disorders.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To provide insights into male infertility.
In men who experience symptoms of hormonal imbalance.
In females with male traits, such as excessive body hair (hirsutism) or irregular or absent periods.
To monitor treatment response in individuals with abnormal testosterone.
In individuals undergoing hormone replacement therapy.
In individuals taking medicines that affect testosterone levels.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Testosterone Free.name: Testosterone Free
Testosterone Free.about: The Testosterone Free Test measures the amount of free (unbound to any other substance) testosterone, a male sex hormone, in the blood. This test is used to diagnose conditions such as decreased sex drive, infertility, erectile dysfunction in men, and irregular menstrual periods in women. It can also be utilized to track hormone levels in individuals receiving testosterone replacement therapy.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: In cases of male infertility, to provide insights into potential contributing factors and guide treatment.
In men who experience symptoms of hormonal imbalance, such as low libido, fatigue, mood disturbances, and muscle weakness.
In females with male traits such as excessive body hair (hirsutism) or irregular or absent periods.
To monitor treatment response in individuals with abnormal testosterone levels or those undergoing hormone replacement therapy.
In individuals taking medicines that may affect their testosterone levels.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Testosterone Total & Free.name: Testosterone Total & Free
Testosterone Total & Free.about: A Testosterone Total & Free test measures the total and free forms of testosterone, a primary male sex hormone, in the blood. Testosterone is present in both men and women, but the levels are significantly higher in men. It helps detect conditions like infertility, erectile dysfunction, early or delayed puberty in males, and menstrual irregularities or hormonal issues in females. This test may also be used to track hormone levels in individuals receiving testosterone replacement therapy.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: In cases of male infertility, to provide insights into potential contributing factors and guide treatment.
In men who experience symptoms of hormonal imbalance, such as low libido, fatigue, mood disturbances, and muscle weakness.
In females with male traits such as excessive body hair (hirsutism) or irregular or absent periods.
To monitor treatment response in individuals with abnormal testosterone levels or those undergoing hormone replacement therapy.
In individuals taking medicines that may affect their testosterone levels.

prepInfo.title: Specify age and sex on the test request form.

Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulphate.name: Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulphate
Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulphate.about: A Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulphate Test evaluates the level of dehydroepiandrosterone sulphate (DHEAS), a steroid hormone produced by the adrenal glands, two small glands located above your kidneys. This hormone plays a role in producing male and female sex hormones. This test is often done to assess adrenal function and diagnose certain conditions related to hormone imbalance.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To evaluate the function of adrenal glands.
To help diagnose congenital adrenal hyperplasia and enlargement of the adrenal glands (hyperplasia) in adults.
To investigate adrenal tumors, which can impact hormone production.
To identify hormonal imbalances, especially when there is an overproduction or underproduction of DHEAS.
In babies with ambiguous genitalia, to understand potential underlying conditions.
To assess the onset of puberty in both boys and girls.
As a part of investigation for hormonal disorders like Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome (PCOS) in females.
To investigate whether hormonal factors contribute to excessive hair growth (hirsutism) or hair loss (alopecia) in females.
As a part of fertility assessment to explore potential factors affecting reproductive health.
To identify androgen-related problems such as virilization in females.
To help in the differential diagnosis of Cushing syndrome.
To monitor the treatment response that may affect adrenal function.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Sex Hormone Binding Globulin.name: Sex Hormone Binding Globulin
Sex Hormone Binding Globulin.about: The Sex Hormone Binding Globulin Test is a blood test that measures the level of sex hormone binding globulin (SHBG), a protein made mostly in the liver. It binds to three sex hormones: testosterone, dihydrotestosterone (DHT), and estrogen. This test is usually done in both men and women when there are signs and symptoms of having too much or too little of the sex hormone testosterone.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To assess the levels of testosterone and estrogen in the blood
To help diagnose androgen-related conditions such as hypogonadism, polycystic ovarian syndrome, and thyroid disorders
To investigate symptoms of hormonal imbalance such as irregular menstrual cycles, decreased sex drive, infertility, excess facial and body hair (hirsutism), acne etc in both men and women
To monitor the effectiveness of hormonal replacement therapy(HRT) or other treatments affecting hormone levels
In conjunction with other hormonal tests to evaluate the status of your sex hormones

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Cortisol, Serum (Morning Sample).name: Cortisol, Serum (Morning Sample)
Cortisol, Serum (Morning Sample).about: The Cortisol, Serum (Morning Sample) Test is a blood test that measures the level of cortisol, a steroid hormone produced by the adrenal gland. It is typically done in the morning when cortisol levels are at their peak, helping diagnose conditions associated with adrenal gland functioning, such as Cushing’s syndrome or Addison’s disease.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To check for Cushing’s syndrome, where the body makes too much cortisol, and Addison’s disease, where the body does not make enough.
To see how the body is responding to stress by measuring cortisol levels.
To check how well the pituitary gland is working, since it controls cortisol production.
To monitor cortisol levels in people who are taking hormone therapy.
To find the reason for symptoms like unexplained weight gain or loss, tiredness, or mood swings, which may be caused by abnormal cortisol levels.
To help understand sleep problems like insomnia.
As part of health checkups, look for conditions linked to cortisol, like metabolic syndrome.

prepInfo.title: Recommended Timings: Morning: 7-10 am.

PTH (Intact Parathyroid Hormone).name: PTH (Intact Parathyroid Hormone)
PTH (Intact Parathyroid Hormone).about: A PTH (Intact Parathyroid Hormone) Test test assesses the level of parathyroid hormone (PTH) that plays a crucial role in regulating calcium and phosphorus levels in the body. This test helps evaluate parathyroid gland function and primarily diagnose conditions related to calcium imbalance.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A PTH (Intact Parathyroid Hormone) Test test is done:
To evaluate parathyroid gland function.
To diagnose conditions associated with calcium imbalance.
To diagnose and monitor disorders like hypoparathyroidism or hyperparathyroidism.
To monitor patients with chronic kidney disease.
To assess bone health and risk of osteoporosis.
To determine the effectiveness of ongoing treatment for parathyroid disorders.
To monitor surgical treatment for hyperparathyroidism.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting (8-12 hrs) is required. Do not eat or drink anything except water before the test.

Growth Hormone.name: Growth Hormone
Growth Hormone.about: The Growth Hormone Test test is a blood test that measures the level of growth hormone (GH) which is produced by the pituitary gland and helps regulate growth, metabolism and overall body composition. This test helps diagnose GH-related disorders such as Growth Hormone Deficiency (GHD), Acromegaly, Gigantism, pituitary tumors etc.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To assess growth hormone levels in children showing growth abnormalities.
To diagnose conditions like acromegaly or growth hormone deficiency in adults.
To investigate symptoms such as unexplained weight gain, fatigue, or changes in body composition.
To monitor the effectiveness of growth hormone replacement therapy.
In conjunction with other hormonal tests to evaluate overall endocrine function.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting (8-12 hrs) is required. Do not eat or drink anything except water before the test.
Patient should be at complete rest 30 minutes prior to sample collection.

Urine Pregnancy Test.name: Urine Pregnancy Test
Urine Pregnancy Test.about: The Urine Pregnancy Test detects the presence of the hormone human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) in urine. This test is a Rapid Immuno-chromatographic test performed in the laboratory. This hormone is typically present shortly after conception, making the test a reliable approach for early pregnancy detection.

sampleInfo.title: Urine
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will provide a clean, sterile container for you to collect a urine sample.

why.title: To verify pregnancy by identifying the presence of hCG in urine.
To help distinguish between normal menstrual irregularities and potential pregnancy.
To facilitate discussions about prenatal care, lifestyle changes, and health considerations during pregnancy.
To aid in understanding fertility issues and potential next steps for those trying to conceive.

prepInfo.title: Collect a First morning/Random urine sample in a sealed and sterile screw-capped container provided by our sample collection professional. (First morning sample is preferred)
Note: The Urine Pregnancy Test (UPT) will be performed in the laboratory. Kindly provide a fresh urine sample at the time of sample collection.
Clinical history is required.
Provide date of last menstrual period (LMP) of the patient

HCG Beta Total Quantitative, Maternal.name: HCG Beta Total Quantitative, Maternal
HCG Beta Total Quantitative, Maternal.about: The HCG Beta Total Quantitative, Maternal Test test measures the level of the hormone human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) that is produced during pregnancy and can be detected as early as 10 to 12 days after conceiving. This test is also done to support the diagnosis of abnormal conditions unrelated to pregnancy that can raise hCG levels.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. In Symptomatic Individuals
To confirm or monitor pregnancy in women with symptoms such as:
Missed or delayed menstrual period
Nausea and vomiting (morning sickness)
Breast tenderness
Fatigue or dizziness
Abdominal cramps
Frequent urination
B. In High-Risk Groups
Women with a history of recurrent miscarriages
Individuals undergoing fertility treatments
Individuals with prior ectopic pregnancy
Women with a history of molar pregnancy (hydatidiform mole)
C. In Individuals With Lifestyle-Related Risks
Smokers or substance users with suspected early pregnancy
Women exposed to reproductive toxins or workplace hazards
Those under high physical or emotional stress during conception
D. In Individuals With Related Health Conditions
Suspected gestational trophoblastic disease (e.g., choriocarcinoma)
Monitoring HCG levels after treatment for trophoblastic disease
E. In Routine Follow-Ups
To monitor the progression of pregnancy in the early weeks
To track falling HCG levels after miscarriage or abortion
To follow up after treatment for ectopic or molar pregnancy
F.. In Prenatal Genetic Screening
1. As Dual Marker Test (First Trimester Screening)
Down Syndrome (Trisomy 21)
Edwards Syndrome (Trisomy 18)
2. Quad Marker Test (Second Trimester Screening)
Neural tube defects (e.g., spina bifida)
Down Syndrome (Trisomy 21)
Trisomy 18

prepInfo.title:
Please provide the first day of your last menstrual period (LMP). 
Note: LMP is optional and not required for the test, but it may help interpret the result based on the stage of pregnancy.

measures.name: HCG Beta Total Quantitative, Maternal Test

Dengue Fever NS1 Antigen.name: Dengue Fever NS1 Antigen
Dengue Fever NS1 Antigen.about: The Dengue Fever NS1 Antigen helps to detect dengue, a viral infection caused by the dengue virus (DENV). This test detects the presence of the dengue NS1 antigen, a protein produced by DENV. It is most effective during the first few days after the onset of symptoms, enabling early diagnosis and timely medical management to prevent severe complications.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: A. For Confirming Diagnosis
To detect the dengue NS1 antigen in blood
To confirm dengue infection in the early phase
To guide further testing, such as dengue IgM/IgG
If you have symptoms like fever, body pain, or rash
B. For High-Risk Groups
Children and elderly individuals
People with weakened immunity
Residents or travelers in dengue outbreak zones

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Dengue Fever, IgG & IgM.name: Dengue Fever, IgG & IgM
Dengue Fever, IgG & IgM.about: A Dengue Fever, IgG & IgM test is performed to check the presence of IgG and IgM antibodies produced by the immune system of an affected individual in response to dengue infection. It helps determine the stage of disease, differentiate between recent and past infections, and aid in the appropriate and timely management of the infection.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: If an individual experiences symptoms suggestive of dengue fever, such as fever, body pain, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, rash, and pain behind the eyes.
For diagnosis and management of dengue infection.
To differentiate between current and past dengue infection.
In case of recent travel history to dengue endemic areas.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Dengue Fever Antigen NS1, IgG & IgM.name: Dengue Fever Antigen NS1, IgG & IgM
Dengue Fever Antigen NS1, IgG & IgM.about: A Dengue Fever Antigen NS1, IgG & IgM test plays a crucial role in diagnosing dengue, a viral infection caused by the dengue virus. This test measures the levels of the NS1 antigen and IgG and IgM antibodies in the blood. Together, they help determine the stage of infection, differentiate between recent and past infections, and aid in the appropriate and timely management of the infection.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: If an individual experiences symptoms suggestive of dengue fever, such as fever, body pain, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, rash, and pain behind the eyes.
For diagnosis and management of dengue infection.
To differentiate between current and past dengue infection.
In case of recent travel history to dengue endemic areas.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Malarial Antigen (Vivax & Falciparum) De.name: Malarial Antigen (Vivax & Falciparum) Detection
Malarial Antigen (Vivax & Falciparum) De.about: A Malarial Antigen (Vivax & Falciparum) Detection test screens for specific malarial antigens in the blood associated with two common types of malaria parasites, Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium falciparum. It aids in the identification of malarial infections by detecting the proteins produced by these parasites.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: In case of symptoms suggestive of malaria such as fever with chills, and other flu-like symptoms.
After potential exposure to mosquitoes, especially in malaria-endemic areas, even without symptoms.
To identify which type of Plasmodium parasite is causing the infection.
As a part of a fever panel to determine if malaria is the cause of your fever.
To assess the effectiveness of malaria treatment.
As a part of preventive screening especially before traveling to malaria-prone areas.
As a part of periodic health check, if you live in or often visit high-risk malaria regions.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Widal Test (Slide Agglutination).name: Widal Test (Slide Agglutination)
Widal Test (Slide Agglutination).about: The Widal Test (Slide Agglutination) helps detect typhoid and paratyphoid fever, collectively known as enteric fever, by identifying the antibodies against two antigens (O & H) of typhoid-causing bacteria, Salmonella typhi. Early detection of enteric fever is crucial to prevent severe complications like intestinal bleeding or perforation.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To detect typhoid fever.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Salmonella Typhi (Typhidot) IgG & IgM.name: Salmonella Typhi (Typhidot) IgG & IgM
Salmonella Typhi (Typhidot) IgG & IgM.about: A Salmonella Typhi (Typhidot) IgG & IgM test is done to detect the presence or absence of antibodies (IgG and IgM) against Salmonella typhi, the bacteria that causes typhoid fever. This is a rapid, easy-to-perform, user-friendly, accurate, and reliable test to identify a typhoid infection. Testing is important as some infected individuals may not exhibit any symptoms yet can spread the infection to others.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As part of the fever panel.
In case of signs or symptoms of typhoid (enteric) fever, such as headache, high fever, abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, or skin rashes.

To screen people who are at a high risk of contracting typhoid fever, such as those who have just returned from a trip to a region where the illness is widespread or who have recently come in contact with infected people.
To evaluate a patient’s response to typhoid fever treatment, and to determine treatment effectiveness.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Chikungunya, IgM.name: Chikungunya, IgM
Chikungunya, IgM.about: A Chikungunya, IgM test is a blood test that helps to detect the presence of specific antibodies immunoglobulin M (IgM) produced by the body in response to the Chikungunya virus. It is used to screen a recent infection and helps in timely intervention.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: If you are experiencing symptoms such as high fever, joint pain, joint swelling, fatigue, rash, and muscle pain
To detect antibodies early for an early diagnosis of Chikungunya virus
After recent travel to Chikungunya endemic areas.
To monitor the spread and prevalence of the chikungunya virus in a population.
For pregnant women with symptoms, to manage and monitor the impact on mother and baby.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Scrub Typhus - IgM antibody.name: Scrub Typhus - IgM antibody
Scrub Typhus - IgM antibody.about: The Scrub Typhus - IgM antibody is a blood test used to detect immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibodies. These antibodies are specific to Orientia tsutsugamushi, the bacteria responsible for scrub typhus. This test helps identify recent or active infections, allowing for early medical intervention.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To detect early or active scrub typhus infection.
When symptoms such as fever, rash, and muscle pain suggest scrub typhus.
After travel or exposure to areas where scrub typhus is endemic.
To help differentiate scrub typhus from other febrile illnesses.
To aid in the evaluation of the response to the treatment for scrub typhus.
To detect any reinfection or relapse of scrub typhus.
To assess the risk of complications associated with scrub typhus, such as organ damage or meningitis.

prepInfo.title: Clinical history is preferred.

Leptospira - IgM antibody.name: Leptospira - IgM antibody
Leptospira - IgM antibody.about: The Leptospira - IgM antibody test is a blood test that helps diagnose leptospirosis, a bacterial infection commonly spread through contact with the urine of infected animals or contaminated water and soil. This test measures IgM antibodies in the blood against Leptospira bacteria.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To diagnose early-stage leptospirosis by identifying Leptospira-specific IgM antibodies.
To support diagnosis in individuals with symptoms of acute febrile illness after potential exposure.
To differentiate leptospirosis from other illnesses causing similar symptoms (e.g., dengue, malaria, typhoid).
To guide timely treatment and prevent complications.

prepInfo.title: Clinical history is preferred.

CRP (C-Reactive Protein), Quantitative.name: CRP (C-Reactive Protein), Quantitative
CRP (C-Reactive Protein), Quantitative.about: The CRP (C-Reactive Protein), Quantitative Test is a simple blood test that measures the level of CRP, a protein produced by the liver, in the body. Usually, the CRP levels in the blood are usually low. However, they rise when there is inflammation in the body.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: Detect and monitor infections or autoimmune diseases like arthritis or lupus.
Detect and monitor conditions like inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) or pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).
Assess inflammation from tissue injury or damage.
Track how well treatments work for chronic inflammatory diseases.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Procalcitonin.name: Procalcitonin
Procalcitonin.about: A Procalcitonin Test test measures the level of procalcitonin (PCT), a type of protein that the body produces in response to bacterial infections. This test helps distinguish between bacterial and viral infections, offering valuable insights about the nature of the infection. By doing so, it contributes to more effective and targeted treatment decisions.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To help diagnose severe bacterial infections or sepsis.
To differentiate between bacterial and viral infections.
To help indicate systemic infections affecting the entire body.
To help monitor the therapeutic response to antibacterial therapy.
For individuals at a heightened risk of infections, including infants, children, older adults, or those with weakened immune systems or underlying illnesses.
To assess the risk of progression from critical illness to severe sepsis and septic shock.
To diagnose kidney infections in children with urinary tract infections.
To identify secondary bacterial infection in individuals with tissue damage from trauma surgery, or viral illnesses like pneumonia.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

HIV Combo (Antigen And Antibody) Test.name: HIV Combo (Antigen And Antibody) Test
HIV Combo (Antigen And Antibody) Test.about: An HIV Combo (Antigen And Antibody) Test is an advanced (fourth-generation) screening test. It is used for simultaneous detection of HIV p24 antigen and antibodies to human immunodeficiency virus type 1 and type 2 (HIV-1/HIV-2) in blood. The test helps in the early diagnosis of an HIV infection. It does not distinguish between the detection of HIV p24 antigen, HIV-1 antibody, or HIV-2 antibody reactivity.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To screen for HIV infection at an early stage.
To check your HIV status if you are pregnant or planning to conceive.
If some has been diagnosed with tuberculosis, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or any other sexually transmitted disease (STD).
To confirm if HIV is present in donated blood or plasma.

prepInfo.title: A duly filled Consent form for HIV testing & Pre-test counselling (Annexure - CR/01) is mandatory.

RPR (Rapid Plasma Reagin).name: RPR (Rapid Plasma Reagin)
RPR (Rapid Plasma Reagin).about: The RPR (Rapid Plasma Reagin) Test is a blood test used to detect syphilis, a sexually transmitted disease (STD). It detects the presence of antibodies produced by the body in response to the syphilis infection. This test is used for initial syphilis screening and monitoring the effectiveness of treatment in individuals diagnosed with the disease.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To screen for syphilis in people having symptoms of sexually transmitted infections.

To screen people who are at risk of exposure to syphilis, such as having another STD or HIV infection, homosexual men having a sexual partner diagnosed with syphilis, or indulging in high-risk sexual activity.
To screen pregnant women for syphilis.
To monitor the ongoing treatment response for syphilis.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Mantoux Test.name: Mantoux Test
Mantoux Test.about: The Mantoux Test, also called the Tuberculin (TB) Skin Test (TST), is used to detect if a person has been exposed to tuberculosis (TB) bacteria. It involves injecting a small amount of purified protein derivative (PPD) tuberculin just beneath the skin on the forearm. The test measures the immune system’s response to this injection by checking for a raised, hard swelling (induration) at the site after 48 to 72 hours.

why.title: Detect latent TB in people without symptoms
Help diagnose TB in symptomatic patients along with other tests
Screen high-risk individuals
Support public health measures to reduce TB spread
Monitor those with past TB exposure

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.
Do not scratch, rub, or apply creams to the injection site after the test, as this may affect the results. Keep the area clean and dry.

Culture Aerobic Blood (Automated), Adult.name: Culture Aerobic Blood (Automated), Adult
Culture Aerobic Blood (Automated), Adult.about: The Culture Aerobic Blood (Automated), Adult test detects and identifies the presence of aerobic microorganisms in the blood of adults (above 12 years of age). It helps diagnose bacterial infections of the blood (bacteremia), sepsis, and other infections that can become fatal if not timely treated. On identification of the organism, antibiotic susceptibilities are performed to aid in the selection of appropriate antibiotics for treatment.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: In case signs or symptoms of infection/sepsis, including fever, rapid heart rate, nausea, confusion, and reduced frequency of urination are noticed.
In critically ill patients, individuals with recent infections, those with a history of recent surgery or valve replacement, or when there is a high risk of systemic infections
To monitor response to an ongoing treatment.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Helicobacter Pylori, IgG.name: Helicobacter Pylori, IgG
Helicobacter Pylori, IgG.about: The Helicobacter Pylori, IgG test detects IgG antibodies against Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori), a bacterium that affects the stomach and intestine. It helps identify past H. Pylori infections and understand the immune response.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: The Helicobacter Pylori, IgG test is done:
To diagnose any previous H. pylori infection.
When there are symptoms of H.pylori infection.
In individuals with a history of gastric ulcers or stomach cancer.
To monitor treatment response.
To help prevent complications like ulcers or cancer.

prepInfo.title: Specimen Type, Site, Clinical History, and Clinician number for notification are required

TORCH Profile 8 Parameters.name: TORCH Profile 8 Parameters
TORCH Profile 8 Parameters.about: The TORCH Profile 8 Parameters is a comprehensive screening to detect infections that can affect pregnancy and fetal development. It includes tests for Toxoplasma gondii ( both IgG and IgM) , Rubella virus (both IgG and IgM), Herpes Simplex Virus type 1 & 2 (both IgG and IgM), and Cytomegalovirus (both IgG and IgM). This profile helps identify and manage potential risks associated with these infections.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: As a part of preconception screening to identify any pre-existing immunity or recent infections against TORCH pathogens, ensuring a healthy start to pregnancy.
For pregnant women to assess exposure to TORCH infections, as certain infections have implications for fetal health.
For women undergoing prenatal screening when fetal anomalies are detected , helping to understand if TORCH infections could be the contributing factor.
When individuals exhibit unexplained symptoms such as fever, rash, or flu-like symptoms , prompting investigation into potential TORCH infections.
When there is a known or suspected exposure to TORCH infections, such as contact with individuals diagnosed with these infections.
For those individuals with weakened immune systems, as they are more susceptible to TORCH infections.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Rheumatoid Factor - Quantitative.name: Rheumatoid Factor - Quantitative
Rheumatoid Factor - Quantitative.about: The Rheumatoid Factor - Quantitative Test test measures the amount of rheumatoid factor (RF) in your blood. This test detects or monitors autoimmune conditions (in which the immune system mistakenly attacks healthy cells and tissues), such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), Sjögren's syndrome, and systemic lupus erythematosus.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: If there are signs and symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis, such as pain, warmth, swelling, morning stiffness in the joints, nodules under the skin, etc.
To diagnose autoimmune diseases, such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or Sjogren’s syndrome.
To determine the severity of RA. Higher levels of RF suggest a more aggressive form of the disease that may require specific therapy.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Anti-CCP Antibody.name: Anti-CCP Antibody
Anti-CCP Antibody.about: The Anti-CCP Antibody test helps diagnose rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and tells it apart from other types of arthritis. It looks for anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (Anti-CCP) antibodies in your blood. These antibodies are linked to autoimmune diseases like RA and are often present in the early stages.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To detect rheumatoid arthritis, understand how serious it is, and how it might progress.
