If you have joint pain, swelling, stiffness, or other signs of arthritis.
To distinguish RA from other types of arthritis or autoimmune diseases.
To track the progress of RA in people already diagnosed.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Anti Nuclear Antibody, EIA.name: Anti Nuclear Antibody, EIA
Anti Nuclear Antibody, EIA.about: An Anti Nuclear Antibody, EIA test helps to identify antinuclear antibodies (ANA) in the blood. These antibodies often attack your body's own tissues specifically targeting each cell's nucleus. This test helps diagnose autoimmune disorders such as lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, and scleroderma among others.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: An Anti Nuclear Antibody, EIA test is done:
To detect autoimmune disorders such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), Rheumatoid arthritis (RA), etc.
When individuals exhibit symptoms such as joint pain, fatigue, skin rashes, inflammation, etc associated with certain autoimmune conditions.
To identify the possible presence of autoimmune connective tissue disorders other than SLE such as Polymyositis, Scleroderma, Sjögren's syndrome, etc.
To monitor the progression and severity of autoimmune disorders over time.
For risk assessment in individuals with a family history of autoimmune conditions.
For a comprehensive health evaluation, especially when systemic autoimmune involvement is suspected.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Anti ds-DNA Antibody, EIA.name: Anti ds-DNA Antibody, EIA
Anti ds-DNA Antibody, EIA.about: The Anti ds-DNA Antibody, EIA test identifies the presence of autoantibodies against double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) in the blood. It helps diagnose autoimmune disorders such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and other autoimmune-related conditions, guiding diagnosis and treatment.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To help diagnose systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and other related autoimmune disorders.
When individuals present with symptoms such as joint pain, skin rashes, kidney issues, and fatigue, which may be associated with certain autoimmune conditions.
To assess the severity and progression of autoimmune diseases over time.
For individuals with a family history of autoimmune disorders as part of a risk assessment.
For a comprehensive health evaluation, especially when systemic autoimmune involvement is suspected.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

HLA - B27 Detection by Flowcytometry.name: HLA - B27 Detection by Flowcytometry
HLA - B27 Detection by Flowcytometry.about: An HLA - B27 Detection by Flowcytometry is a blood test that helps to identify the presence of Human Leukocyte Antigen B27(HLA B-27), a specific type of protein that is present on the surface of white blood cells (WBCs) that helps the body's immune system tell the difference between its own cells and foreign/harmful substances. This test can help diagnose autoimmune disorders associated with HLA B-27 antigen.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To detect inflammatory conditions, especially those affecting the joints and spine
In case of symptoms such as chronic joint pain, stiffness, and inflammation in the lower back, hips, neck, and chest suggestive of arthritis
In case of uveitis (painful inflammation of eyes) particularly in males experiencing symptoms that begin in their early 30s
In individuals who have a family history of autoimmune diseases associated with HLA-B27 gene
In individuals who have to undergo an organ transplant procedure to assess the compatibility between the donor and the recipient
To monitor the progression of disease in individuals with pre-existing autoimmune disorders
In children, showing symptoms of juvenile arthritis associated with the HLA B-27 gene

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Anti Streptolysin O Titer.name: Anti Streptolysin O Titer
Anti Streptolysin O Titer.about: The Anti Streptolysin O Titer Test is a blood test that measures the levels of antibodies against streptolysin O, a toxin produced by group A streptococcus bacteria. It helps diagnose recent streptococcal infections and related complications, such as rheumatic fever and acute glomerulonephritis.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To confirm exposure to Streptococcus pyogenes bacteria.
To help diagnose rheumatic fever as indicated by elevated ASO levels.
To monitor the effectiveness of antibiotic treatment over time against streptococcal bacterial infections.
To investigate potential complications of streptococcal infections such as acute glomerulonephritis.
For risk assessment of autoimmune disorders associated with streptococcus bacterial infection like rheumatic fever or post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

C3 Complement.name: C3 Complement
C3 Complement.about: The C3 Complement Test is a blood test that measures the levels of C3, a protein that plays a critical role in the immune system's complement cascade (a series of reactions in the blood which help the body's immune system clear pathogens and damaged cells). It helps diagnose autoimmune diseases, infections and also assess immune system health.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To diagnose autoimmune diseases like lupus or rheumatoid arthritis.

When unexplained symptoms are present, including persistent fatigue, joint pain or swelling, skin rashes (especially a butterfly-shaped rash across the cheeks and nose), fever, or other signs suggestive of autoimmune disorders.
To evaluate the functioning of the immune system,particularly in the presence of inflammation or infection.
To detect chronic infections or inflammatory conditions that might affect complement protein levels.
To monitor the progression or remission in individuals with known autoimmune conditions.
To differentiate between types of immune responses or phases of disease activity.
If there are known risk factors like a family history of complement deficiencies or autoimmune diseases.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

C4 Complement.name: C4 Complement
C4 Complement.about: The C4 Complement Test test is a blood test that assesses levels of complement component 4 (C4), a protein involved in the immune system's complement cascade. This test helps detect autoimmune diseases, infections, and other conditions with dysfunction in the immune system.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To assist in diagnosing autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), vasculitis, etc.
To find the cause of unexplained symptoms such as joint pain, swelling, skin rashes, and fatigue, which might suggest autoimmune or inflammatory diseases.
To monitor the functioning of the immune system, especially in chronic infections or inflammation.
To assess disease progression or remission in patients with autoimmune disease.
To check for renal involvement of lupus nephritis or other autoimmune disorders.
To check whether either an infection or inflammation is lowering complement protein levels.
To investigate any family history of complement deficiencies or autoimmune diseases.

prepInfo.title: Overnight fasting is preferred but not mandatory. Follow the doctor's instructions regarding fasting requirements.

Rheumatoid Arthritis Profile.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis Profile
Rheumatoid Arthritis Profile.about: The Rheumatoid Arthritis profile helps to detect an autoimmune disorder called rheumatoid arthritis. This disease occurs when your immune system attacks the healthy tissues of your joints of hands or legs. These tests can be used if you have risk factors like a family history of rheumatoid arthritis or obesity. You may get these tests done when you have symptoms such as pain, stiffness, tenderness in the joints of the hands and legs, weight loss, fever, fatigue, and weakness. These tests detect rheumatoid factor with IgM antibody, anticitrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA), and other anti-nuclear antibodies (RA33, SS-A/Ro60, SSA-A/Ro52, SS-B/La, and ds-DNA). Measures such as avoiding smoking may help lower your chance of rheumatoid arthritis progression.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

Total IgE.name: Total IgE
Total IgE.about: Total IgE, also known as the Immunoglobulin E test, helps in determining allergic reactions and immune responses by measuring the level of Immunoglobulin E (IgE) antibodies present in the blood. It detects multiple allergies, ranging from seasonal allergies, food allergies, and insect sting allergies to parasitic diseases and certain immune illnesses.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: If you experience allergy symptoms such as itchy or watery eyes, swelling, shortness of breath, skin rash, congestion, or sneezing.
To track and monitor treatment progress and effectiveness
If a parasitic infection or allergic respiratory disease is suspected.
In individuals with a family history of allergies.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Allergy Panel - Animal.name: Allergy Panel - Animal
Allergy Panel - Animal.about: The Allergy Panel - Animal is a set of blood tests that check for allergies to various animal-derived allergens, such as cat, dog, cow, horse, and guinea pig dander. It looks for specific allergy-related antibodies (IgE) using the ImmunoCAP method, helping doctors plan management.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To identify if allergic reactions are caused by animal dander and epithelial cells.
To evaluate the severity and source of allergic symptoms.
To monitor sensitization trends in some cases
To personalize allergy treatment plans, including medication and immunotherapy.
To assess allergy risk in individuals with a family history of allergies.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Allergy Dust Mite Panel.name: Allergy Dust Mite Panel
Allergy Dust Mite Panel.about: The Allergy Dust Mite Panel is a group of tests that measures specific IgE and total IgE antibodies to common dust mites using the ImmunoCAP method. This panel helps find out if an individual is allergic to dust mites and helps doctors create a treatment plan.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To diagnose allergies triggered by dust mites, particularly Blomia Tropicalis, Dermatophagoides farinae and Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus.
To evaluate the cause of allergic symptoms like nasal congestion, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, skin rashes, and wheezing.
To monitor and assess the effectiveness of allergy treatments.
To identify allergens in individuals with a family history of allergies or asthma.

prepInfo.title: No special preparation is required.

Allergy Panel - Nuts.name: Allergy Panel - Nuts
Allergy Panel - Nuts.about: The Allergy Panel - Nuts comprises a group of tests that measure specific immunoglobulin IgE antibodies against various types of allergens, including almond, walnut, peanut, cashew, pecanut, hazelnut, Brazil nut, coconut, and pistachio, using the ImmunoCAP method. This panel helps identify potential nut allergies and helps doctors tailor targeted treatment plans.

sampleInfo.title: Blood

PSA (Prostate Specific Antigen) Total.name: PSA (Prostate Specific Antigen) Total
PSA (Prostate Specific Antigen) Total.about: The PSA (Prostate Specific Antigen) Total Test measures the total amount of PSA, a protein produced by the prostate gland that helps liquefy the semen in males. This test helps identify conditions like prostate inflammation (prostatitis), enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH), prostate cancer, etc.

Prostate Specific Antigen (Free) PSA.name: Prostate Specific Antigen (Free) PSA
Prostate Specific Antigen (Free) PSA.about: The Prostate Specific Antigen (Free) PSA Test test measures the levels of unbound or free prostate-specific antigen (PSA) in blood. It helps in differentiating between prostate cancer and other prostate-related conditions, such as prostate inflammation and an enlarged prostate. This test is often used in conjunction with the total PSA (free and bound PSA) test and other diagnostic tools to assess prostate health.

CA125 (Cancer Antigen 125).name: CA125 (Cancer Antigen 125)
CA125 (Cancer Antigen 125).about: A CA125 (Cancer Antigen 125) Test measures the amount of protein CA125 (Cancer Antigen 125) in blood. It is a tumor marker used to monitor certain cancers (particularly ovarian cancer) during and after therapy. In some high-risk individuals, the test may be used to look for early signs of an ovarian tumor. Serial measurements help to detect cancer recurrence and predict response to therapy. This test is not considered useful for cancer detection screening in the normal population.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

To monitor the effectiveness of ovarian cancer treatment.

CA15.3.name: CA15.3
CA15.3.about: The CA15.3 Test measures the glycoprotein marker Cancer Antigen 15.3 in the blood. It is primarily used as a tumor marker for breast cancer. It is an important tool to monitor patients with breast cancer, to know treatment effectiveness in patients undergoing cancer treatment, and to monitor the relapse or metastasis status (spread to other parts of the body).

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To check the progress of the disease and efficacy of the treatment if you are diagnosed with breast cancer
To check for further progress or recurrence of the cancer if you are treated for breast cancer.

prepInfo.title: Provide brief clinical history/doctor's prescription at the time of sample collection.

CA19.9.name: CA19.9
CA19.9.about: A CA19.9 Test test, also known as carbohydrate antigen 19.9, is a blood test used to measure the levels of CA 19.9 protein in the blood. CA 19.9 is a tumor marker that may be increased in individuals with certain types of cancer, particularly pancreatic cancer and some non-cancerous conditions. This test helps diagnose cancer, monitor cancer treatment response, and detect cancer recurrence post-treatment.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

To monitor cancer progression and assess the treatment response.
To detect potential cancer recurrence.
To monitor other non-cancerous conditions like pancreatitis, cirrhosis, etc, or various other cancers, including colorectal, gastric, hepatobiliary, and ovarian cancer.

prepInfo.title: Provide brief clinical history/ doctor's prescription at the time of sample collection.

Carcino Embryonic Antigen.name: Carcino Embryonic Antigen
Carcino Embryonic Antigen.about: The Carcino Embryonic Antigen Test or CEA test is used to measure the level of CEA, a protein that can be present in higher amounts in certain types of cancers, particularly the adenocarcinoma of the large intestine and rectum (colorectal cancers). However, it may also be used to monitor other cancers, such as breast, lung, thyroid, and pancreatic cancer.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: To monitor cancer treatment, including response to therapy and recurrence.
As an indicator of the amount of cancer or size of tumor present (tumor burden).
To assist in cancer staging.
As a follow-up to a positive screening test for cancer.

Alpha Feto Protein, Tumour Marker.name: Alpha Feto Protein, Tumour Marker
Alpha Feto Protein, Tumour Marker.about: An Alpha Feto Protein, Tumour Marker Test test measures the amount of a specific protein called Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) in your blood. This protein is synthesized primarily in the liver and yolk sac of the fetus. This test aids in the management of cancers of the liver, ovaries, and testicles. However, AFP testing is not recommended as a screening procedure to detect cancer in the general population.

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: In case cancers of the liver, testicles, or ovaries are suspected.
In the case of cancer-predisposing diseases such as chronic hepatitis or cirrhosis.
At intervals during and after treatment for liver, testicle, or ovarian cancers.

Cancer Marker Profile - Male.name: Cancer Marker Profile - Male
Cancer Marker Profile - Male.about: The Cancer Marker Profile - Male is a comprehensive male cancer marker package designed to support risk assessment, diagnosis support, and long-term monitoring of selected malignancies. It measures multiple tumor markers and hematological parameters that help detect potential malignancy, assess disease burden, and monitor treatment response or recurrence when interpreted alongside other clinical findings.

Urine R/M (Urine Routine & Microscopy).name: Urine R/M (Urine Routine & Microscopy)
Urine R/M (Urine Routine & Microscopy).about: The Urine R/M (Urine Routine & Microscopy) test examines the urine's appearance, concentration, and content. It is done if the doctor suspects kidney disorders, diabetes, and other metabolic conditions. This test is also done as a part of a routine medical examination, pregnancy checkup, or preparation before surgery.

sampleInfo.title: Urine

Frequent urge to urinate

Inadequate fluid intake

prepInfo.title: The urine sample (a minimum quantity of 10 ml urine) must preferably be the first-morning midstream urine (part of urine that comes after the first and before the last stream). Collect the urine sample in a sealed and sterile screw-capped container provided by our sample collection professional. Ensure that the urethral area (from where the urine is passed) is clean & the container doesn't come in contact with your skin. Women are advised not to give the sample during the menstrual period unless prescribed.

Urine Protein (Albumin), Random.name: Urine Protein (Albumin), Random
Urine Protein (Albumin), Random.about: The Urine Protein (Albumin), Random Test test measures the amount of albumin protein present in urine. Normally, the kidneys prevent most proteins from passing into the urine. The presence of albumin in urine may indicate kidney damage or early kidney disease.

sampleInfo.title: Urine
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will provide a clean, sterile container for you to collect a urine sample.

why.title: To help detect early signs of kidney disease
If you have symptoms such as swelling of the feet, ankles, or face that may indicate kidney problems

To monitor kidney function in individuals already diagnosed with kidney disease
During pregnancy, if preeclampsia is suspected
As part of routine health check-ups for individuals at high risk of kidney disease

Microalbumin Creatinine Ratio, Urine.name: Microalbumin Creatinine Ratio, Urine
Microalbumin Creatinine Ratio, Urine.about: The Microalbumin Creatinine Ratio, Urine Test test helps assess kidney function and detect early signs of kidney damage, particularly related to conditions such as diabetes, high blood pressure (hypertension), or other kidney diseases. It measures the very small (or "micro") amounts of albumin and creatinine in the urine.

sampleInfo.title: Urine
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will provide a clean, sterile container for you to collect a urine sample.

why.title: As part of routine health checkups in patients with high blood pressure and type 1 or type 2 diabetes.

To assess overall cardiovascular risk in addition to kidney health.
To monitor treatment response for existing liver and kidney diseases.

Urine Creatinine, Random.name: Urine Creatinine, Random
Urine Creatinine, Random.about: The Urine Creatinine, Random Test test measures the level of creatinine, a waste product, in the urine to evaluate how well your kidneys are functioning. This test can be done as part of routine tests or a kidney function test (KFT) to check your kidney health and detect kidney diseases. It also serves as a useful tool to monitor ongoing treatment response for known kidney disease.

sampleInfo.title: Urine
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will provide a clean, sterile container for you to collect a urine sample.

To evaluate the normal functioning of the kidneys.
To detect any disease affecting the kidneys.
To screen for kidney disease if you have risk factors like obesity, diabetes, high blood pressure, or a family history of kidney disease.
To monitor treatment response of kidney diseases.

To monitor the side effects of certain medications such as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (ibuprofen, naproxen), antibiotics (vancomycin), ACE inhibitors (lisinopril, enalapril), and diuretics (furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide).

Urine Ketone, Qualitative.name: Urine Ketone, Qualitative

It is used to diagnose and monitor conditions such as ketosis, diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), and other metabolic disorders.

sampleInfo.title: Urine

why.title: To diagnose and monitor metabolic conditions such as ketosis and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA).

To assess metabolic health and adjust treatment or dietary plans as per individual health needs.
To detect any early signs of metabolic imbalances that may require medical attention.

PT INR (Prothrombin Time with INR).name: PT INR (Prothrombin Time with INR)
PT INR (Prothrombin Time with INR).about: The PT INR (Prothrombin Time with INR) Test test helps assess the clotting ability of blood. It also provides essential information to manage bleeding or clotting disorders. Additionally, it helps monitor treatment effectiveness if you are on blood-thinning medicines. This test also helps check for clotting function before a scheduled surgery.

sampleInfo.title: Blood

Before planning a surgical procedure.

To aid monitoring in conditions like deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, which involve the formation of harmful blood clots.

Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time.name: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time
Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time.about: An Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time Test test is a screening test that helps evaluate your body's ability to form blood clots. This test is performed to detect bleeding disorders if you have unexplained bleeding or bruising and to monitor ongoing treatment with anticoagulant medicines.

This profile helps diagnose bleeding disorders, such as hemophilia, and monitor the effects of anticoagulant medications.

D-Dimer.name: D-Dimer
D-Dimer.about: A D-Dimer Test detects the presence of D-dimer, a protein fragment produced when a blood clot dissolves in the body. This test helps diagnose and monitor conditions related to blood clot formation, such as deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), stroke, and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC).

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

If symptoms of pulmonary embolism (PE), such as shortness of breath, coughing, back pain, pain in the chest, fast heart rate, and dizziness, are experienced.
If symptoms of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), such as nausea, vomiting, seizures, bleeding gums, and muscular and abdominal pain, are observed.
To rule out blood clotting caused by snake bite, thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS), and stroke.

Fibrinogen.name: Fibrinogen

sampleInfo.title: Blood
sampleInfo.text: Our phlebotomist will draw a blood sample, typically from a vein in your inner elbow.

why.title: If you have unexplained or excessive bleeding or bruising.
To assess your blood’s ability to clot (coagulation status).
To help diagnose bleeding or clotting disorders.
To monitor treatment that affects blood clotting.

To evaluate liver function if you have liver disease or are at risk of liver dysfunction.
If you have a family history of bleeding disorders.

Pre-daycare Package.name: Pre-daycare Package
Pre-daycare Package.about: The Pre-daycare Package is a diagnostic health panel designed to evaluate overall health and organ function before undergoing day care procedures, minor surgeries, or medical interventions. The package comprises pathology tests such as a complete blood count (CBC) that analyzes red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets, helping assess general health and detect infections, anemia, and blood-related abnormalities. A liver function test (LFT) is included to evaluate liver function, liver damage, and liver’s ability to metabolize medications and support normal body functions. The kidney function test (KFT) with electrolytes helps assess kidney health and electrolyte balance for evaluating kidney's ability to filter waste products and maintain fluid balance. Together, these tests provide essential information about a patient's fitness for medical procedures and help identify any underlying conditions that may require attention before treatment. The Pre-daycare Package is enables informed clinical decision-making and improved patient safety.

Women Essential Health Checkup with Smar.about: The Women Essential Health Checkup with Smart Report is a preventive health package designed specifically for women to monitor overall health and help identify common nutritional deficiencies, hormonal imbalances, and metabolic risks at an early stage. The package comprises Complete Blood Count (CBC) to evaluate hemoglobin levels, red blood cells (RBC), white blood cells (WBC), and platelets, supporting assessment of anemia, infections, and overall blood health; Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) to detect underlying inflammation; Fasting Blood Sugar (FBS) and HbA1c to assess blood glucose control and screen for diabetes risk; and a Lipid Profile to evaluate cholesterol levels and cardiovascular health. It also includes Kidney Function Test (KFT) and Liver Function Test (LFT) to assess kidney and liver health; Thyroid Profile Total (T3, T4, and TSH) to evaluate thyroid function; FSH, LH, and Prolactin to assess hormonal balance related to menstrual health, fertility, and reproductive function; Serum Iron Studies, Vitamin B12, Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy), and Serum Calcium to evaluate nutritional status, bone health, and energy levels. The package is supported by a Smart Report, which presents results in an easy-to-understand format with clear health insights. Getting tested with the Women Essential Health Checkup with Smart Report package helps support informed lifestyle, dietary, and wellness decisions for long-term health.

Hormone Health Checkup for Women.name: Hormone Health Checkup for Women
Hormone Health Checkup for Women.about:
The Hormone Health Checkup for Women is a comprehensive hormonal health screening package designed to assess key hormones involved in reproductive, menstrual, ovarian, and thyroid health in women of reproductive age. It provides an overview of hormonal function and may help identify imbalances that can affect menstrual regularity, ovulation, fertility, and overall reproductive health.

The package includes Estradiol (E2) to assess estrogen status and ovarian function; Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) to evaluate follicular development and ovarian function; Luteinising Hormone (LH) to assess hormonal regulation of ovulation; AMH (Anti-Mullerian Hormone) to assess ovarian reserve; Serum Prolactin to identify elevated levels that may affect menstrual cycles and ovulation; and TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone) Ultrasensitive to assess thyroid function, as thyroid abnormalities can influence menstrual and reproductive health. The package also includes Free Androgen Index (FAI), which is calculated using total testosterone and Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG) levels to estimate biologically available androgens and help assess androgen excess in women, which may be associated with symptoms such as irregular periods, acne, or excess facial and body hair.

The Hormone Health Checkup for Women may be considered as part of a general reproductive health assessment, particularly for women experiencing irregular or absent periods, changes in menstrual patterns, difficulty conceiving, or symptoms suggestive of hormonal imbalance. It may also support the evaluation of ovarian function and fertility-related concerns. Getting tested with the Hormone Health Checkup for Women provides a broad assessment of important reproductive and thyroid hormones and can help guide further clinical evaluation when a hormonal or reproductive health concern is suspected.

Children Health Checkup with Smart Repor.name: Children Health Checkup with Smart Report
Children Health Checkup with Smart Repor.about:
The Children Health Checkup with Smart Report is a preventive health package specially designed for children to provide a broad overview of their overall health, growth, nutritional status, blood health, metabolism, and key organ functions. It brings together essential health checks that can help identify nutritional gaps or other health concerns early, supporting timely medical guidance and healthy development.

The package includes a Complete Blood Count (CBC) test and Peripheral Smear Examination to assess different types of blood cells and provide insights into conditions such as anemia, infections, and other blood-related abnormalities. C-Reactive Protein (CRP), Quantitative test helps assess inflammation in the body. To evaluate metabolic health, the package includes a Lipid Profile, which can be done in a non-fasting state to measure cholesterol and triglyceride levels, along with HbA1c (Glycosylated Hemoglobin) to assess average blood sugar levels over the past few months. TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone) Ultrasensitive test helps assess thyroid function, which plays an important role in a child's growth, development, and metabolism. The package also includes Kidney Function Test (KFT) with Electrolytes and Liver Function Test (LFT) to assess kidney and liver function and help evaluate the body's fluid and electrolyte balance. Because adequate nutrition is essential during the growing years, the package evaluates important nutrients through Serum Calcium, Phosphorus, Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy), Basic Iron Studies, Serum Ferritin, and Vitamin B12 tests. These tests provide useful insights into nutrients involved in healthy bones, blood formation, energy metabolism, and normal growth and development. Urine Routine & Microscopy (Urine R/M) is also included to assess urinary health and identify certain abnormalities.

To make the results easier for parents to understand, Children Health Checkup with Smart Report includes an interactive smart health report with simple visuals, pictures, and infographics that present complex health parameters in an easy-to-understand format. Overall, Children Health Checkup with Smart Report provides a comprehensive snapshot of a child's health and nutritional well-being. Periodic preventive health screening, when appropriate for the child's age and individual health needs, can complement routine pediatric care and help parents and healthcare professionals make informed decisions to support healthy growth and development.

Growth and Nutrition Checkup for Childre.name: Growth and Nutrition Checkup for Children
Growth and Nutrition Checkup for Childre.about: The Growth and Nutrition Checkup for Children is a preventive health package designed for children to assess key health parameters related to growth, nutrition, blood health, thyroid function, and overall well-being. The package includes a Complete Blood Count (CBC) test to evaluate red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets, helping assess overall blood health and identify abnormalities such as anemia. Serum Iron Studies Basic and Serum Ferritin evaluate iron status and iron stores, which are important for healthy red blood cell production, growth, and development. The Vitamin Profile, including Vitamin D, Vitamin B12, and Folic Acid, helps assess important nutrients involved in bone health, blood cell formation, and normal growth and development. It may help identify nutritional deficiencies that require further evaluation. Serum Calcium and Serum Phosphorus assess minerals important for healthy bones and normal growth. Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH) Ultrasensitive and Free Thyroxine (FT4) evaluate thyroid function, which plays an important role in a child's growth, metabolism, and development. The package also includes Serum Creatinine to assess kidney function and a Liver Function Test (LFT) to evaluate liver health and function. C-Reactive Protein (CRP), Quantitative measures a marker of inflammation and may help identify an inflammatory response that requires further medical evaluation. Getting tested with the Growth and Nutrition Checkup for Children package provides a broad assessment of nutritional status and key health parameters that support healthy growth and development in children. The results may help identify nutritional deficiencies, anemia, or other abnormalities and support timely medical evaluation when needed.

Allergy and Infection Checkup for Childr.name: Allergy and Infection Checkup for Children
Allergy and Infection Checkup for Childr.about:
The Allergy and Infection Checkup for Children is a preventive health package designed for children to assess key health parameters related to allergies, infections, inflammation, blood health, and nutritional status. The package includes a Complete Blood Count (CBC) test, which evaluates red blood cells (RBCs), platelets, and different types of white blood cells, including the Absolute Eosinophil Count. These parameters help assess overall blood health and may show changes associated with infections, anemia, and allergic or parasitic conditions. C-Reactive Protein (CRP) is a marker of inflammation and may help assess an inflammatory response in the body. Total IgE test measures immunoglobulin E, an antibody commonly associated with allergic conditions and certain parasitic infections, and can support further evaluation of allergy-related symptoms. The package also assesses nutritional factors important for a child's growth and development. Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy) evaluates vitamin D status, which is important for healthy bones and normal growth. Serum Iron Studies Basic and Serum Ferritin help evaluate iron status and iron stores, supporting the assessment of iron deficiency and healthy red blood cell production. Urine R/M (Urine Routine & Microscopy) examines urine for cells, proteins, and other abnormalities and may help identify findings that require further evaluation for urinary health.

Getting tested with the Allergy and Infection Checkup for Children package provides a broad overview of parameters relevant to allergies, infections, inflammation, blood health, and nutritional status in children. The results can support timely medical evaluation and help determine whether further testing is needed.

FBS & PPBS (Fasting & Postprandial Blood.name: FBS & PPBS (Fasting & Postprandial Blood Sugar)
FBS & PPBS (Fasting & Postprandial Blood.about: The FBS & PPBS (Fasting & Postprandial Blood Sugar) test is a group of blood tests that measure fasting blood glucose (FBG) after an overnight fast of 8–12 hours and postprandial blood glucose (PPBG) 2 hours after starting the meal. Together, these tests show how your body processes glucose both before and after meals, helping to predict the risk of diabetes and prediabetes, and monitor diabetes treatment. These tests are commonly included in routine health checkups and diabetes screening tests.

FLU (Influenza) Monitoring panel.name: FLU (Influenza) Monitoring panel
FLU (Influenza) Monitoring panel.about: The FLU (Influenza) Monitoring panel is a comprehensive monitoring package designed to assess key blood, inflammatory, metabolic, kidney, and liver parameters during influenza (flu) infection. It helps monitor the body’s response to influenza and identify changes that may require further medical attention. The package includes a Complete Blood Count (CBC) to assess red blood cells, white blood cells, hemoglobin, and platelets. Changes in these parameters can provide useful information about the body's response to infection and overall blood health. The C-Reactive Protein (CRP), Quantitative test measures the level of inflammation in the body and can help monitor the inflammatory response associated with an ongoing infection. The Random Blood Sugar (RBS) test measures blood glucose levels at the time of testing, as illness and changes in food intake may affect glucose levels. The Kidney Function Test (KFT) with Electrolytes evaluates kidney function and important electrolyte levels, which may be affected during illness, particularly in individuals with reduced fluid intake, vomiting, or dehydration. The Liver Function Test (LFT) assesses liver-related parameters and helps monitor liver function during infection or treatment. The package also includes Urine Routine & Microscopy (Urine R/M), which evaluates the urine for cells, proteins, and other abnormalities that may provide additional information about urinary and kidney health. The FLU (Influenza) Monitoring panel may be useful for individuals who are being monitored during influenza infection, especially when symptoms are persistent, recovery is delayed, or a broader assessment of health is required. Together, these tests can help healthcare professionals monitor blood counts, inflammation, blood glucose, kidney function, electrolyte balance, liver function, and urinary parameters, supporting appropriate follow-up and clinical management.

Chronic Liver Disease Screening Panel wi.name: Chronic Liver Disease Screening Panel with FIB 4

It includes tests that help detect common etiologies of CLD and assess liver function. The panel includes a Liver Function Test (LFT) to evaluate liver function and detect liver injury; Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), Hepatitis B core total antibody, and Hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody to screen for chronic viral hepatitis; Anti-Nuclear Antibody (ANA) by IFA and Immunoglobulin G (IgG) to evaluate autoimmune liver diseases such as autoimmune hepatitis; Complete Blood Count (CBC) to identify blood cell abnormalities commonly associated with chronic liver disease; HbA1c and Lipid Profile to assess diabetes and metabolic risk factors associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD); Comprehensive Serum Iron Studies to detect iron overload disorders such as hereditary hemochromatosis; and Prothrombin Time (PT) with INR to assess the liver's ability to synthesize clotting factors and evaluate disease severity. FIB-4 Index is a scoring tool that uses age, AST, ALT, and platelet count to assess the risk of advanced liver fibrosis, particularly in individuals with chronic liver disease. Getting tested with the Chronic Liver Disease Screening Panel with FIB 4 enables early detection of chronic liver disease, helps identify its underlying cause, assesses disease severity, and supports timely diagnosis, appropriate treatment, and ongoing monitoring to reduce the risk of complications and disease progression.

MTB/NTM DNA Detection by Real Time PCR,.about: The MTB/NTM DNA Detection by Real Time PCR, Extra pulmonary (Blood) test is a molecular diagnostic test that detects the DNA of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) complex and non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) in blood samples. It is primarily used to support the diagnosis of disseminated or extra-pulmonary mycobacterial infections, particularly when bloodstream involvement is suspected or in individuals with weakened immune systems. The test also helps differentiate MTB from NTM, which is clinically important because their treatment and management approaches differ. By directly detecting mycobacterial DNA using real-time PCR, the test can provide rapid and specific results compared with conventional culture-based methods. Results should be interpreted alongside clinical findings, imaging studies, and other relevant laboratory investigations, as detection of mycobacterial DNA alone may not confirm active disease in every case. The MTB/NTM DNA Detection by Real Time PCR, Extra pulmonary (Blood) test supports early identification of mycobacterial infections and can help guide timely and appropriate clinical management.
